title: Zimbabwean tycoon killed in helicopter crash had cultivated presidents as friends
summary: Forensic experts are working to identify bodies from a helicopter crash that killed Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife, and others
story: Forensic experts are working to identify bodies from a helicopter crash that killed Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife, and others

HARARE -- The death in a helicopter crash of Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife and four others has reverberated across government and industry circles on the continent, as investigators began examining what caused the aircraft to go down.
Family spokesperson Herbert Chivayo said the process of identifying the victims was “painful” because of the impact and damage of Wednesday's fiery crash near the capital, Harare.
Wicknell Chivayo was a close ally of Zimbabwe President Emmerson Mnangagwa, and often posted pictures of encounters, including dinners, with heads of state from across Africa.
In a condolence message, Mnangagwa said he was “numbed” by the death, describing Chivayo as “consummately philanthropic.”

The Civil Aviation Authority of Zimbabwe said preliminary observations showed that the helicopter hit the ground, spilling fuel that ignited and burned surrounding grass. Officials said the cause of the crash had yet to be established. A black box was being examined, state broadcaster ZBC News reported. The mangled wreckage lay on the burnt grass as workers from a funeral parlor collected the victims' remains.

The grim scene was a stark contrast to the flamboyant public life the businessman had cultivated. Just hours before the crash, he posted photographs of two luxury vehicles he said he was gifting two of his lawyers, along with $750,000 in cash.

He ended the post with the words: “Saved the best for last.” The giveaways were typical of a man who made extraordinary wealth and generosity central to his public image. Over the years, Chivayo gave away dozens of luxury cars, buses, cash and other gifts to celebrities, church leaders, sports figures, politicians and social media followers, frequently broadcasting his largesse online.
But perhaps more striking than the cars was the company he kept.

Chivayo, 43, nurtured unusually close relationships with African political leaders, regularly posting photographs and videos of encounters with presidents including Mnangagwa, Kenya’s William Ruto, Tanzania’s Samia Suluhu Hassan, Uganda’s Yoweri Museveni, Nigeria’s Bola Tinubu and others.
In August, Chivayo posted a video showing Ruto driving him to a helicopter after attending a traditional engagement ceremony involving the Kenyan president’s daughter.

“I’ve lived large and had many different and exceptionally beautiful experiences in my opulent lifestyle, but certainly this was the first,” Chivayo wrote. Both Ruto, behind the wheel, and Chivayo are seen laughing, with Chivayo's wife grinning from the back seat.
Ruto called him "a dear friend."

Chivayo's Rolls-Royces, private aircraft, designer shoes, luxury watches, shopping trips abroad and multimillion-dollar gifts were a constant presence on social media, while his relationships with presidents gave him visibility far beyond Zimbabwe.
He had received multiple government contracts, some of which drew controversy or allegations of fraud that were thrown out by courts or dismissed by investigating authorities.

On Zimbabwean social media, some people openly celebrated his death, citing his wealth and political connections as reasons for their anger over the country’s economic hardships and allegations surrounding his business dealings. One prominent news website ran the headline: “We are not mourning — Zimbabweans celebrate death of controversial businessman.”
Others pushed back against the celebrations. “What kind of people are we who celebrate someone’s death? It’s un-African,” opposition lawmaker Chalton Hwende wrote.

title: Amazon to invest $1B into communities amid backlash against data center rollouts
summary: Amazon is investing more than $1 billion over the next five years into communities where it operates data centers for education, job training, water preservation projects and other local priorities as it reacts to a growing backlash from politicians an...
story: Amazon is investing more than $1 billion over the next five years into communities where it operates data centers for education, job training, water preservation projects and other local priorities as it reacts to a growing backlash from politicians an...

NEW YORK -- Amazon is investing more than $1 billion over the next five years into communities where it operates data centers for education, job training, water and energy preservation projects and other local priorities as it reacts to a growing backlash from politicians and consumers to the tech industry's rollout of the massive buildings.

According to a blog post on Friday by Matt Garman, Amazon’s CEO of its cloud computing arm, Amazon has already spent more than $1 billion in communities with a large data center presence over the past three years.

Garman also said that Amazon is no longer using nondisclosure agreements with government agencies it works with on its projects, and it said it hosts open houses in communities where it operates to share information about what it's doing. He also warned against the spread of what he believes is misinformation about data centers' impact on the environment and energy rates — and he cited the dangers of over 100 moratoriums against these centers being considered across the country.

“If these measures are enacted, the U.S. could be writing its own losing ticket to this race, and the consequences would last generations,” he wrote. “As a country, we can’t afford to find ourselves in that position. There is urgency to this data center build out because we aren’t the only country that sees the benefits of AI for the economy and national security.”

Garman's pledge comes as data centers, which power artificial intelligence and cloud computing, have become a hot political issue heading into the midterms as tech giants race to invest more money in expanding these infrastructures.

Small, under-the-radar data centers have been around for decades. But the explosion of artificial intelligence chatbots has resulted in data centers that are bigger than anything just about any town has ever seen. Some of them dwarf football stadiums and factories and consume more energy than small cities.

By 2030, data centers will account for nearly 3% of the world’s projected electricity use, with 935 trillion watt-hours, according to a United Nations University report released in June on these buildings' environmental footprint.

Amazon said in July that it now expects to spend $220 billion in capital expenditures in 2026, including on data centers and other technology investments. That’s up from its prior estimate of $200 billion.

President Donald Trump has embraced the building of more data centers, but there is growing wariness from voters. About 6 in 10 Americans support limiting the number of new data centers that can be built, including most Democrats and Republicans.
And a majority of Americans are “extremely” or “very” concerned about the impact of data centers on electricity prices or the water supply in the communities where they are built.

title: Head Start preschools serve parents, too. Under Trump, advocates fear that will change
summary: Parents of Head Start preschoolers are lobbying lawmakers on Capitol Hill, worried proposed changes by the Trump administration threaten the backbone of the federal preschool program
story: Parents of Head Start preschoolers are lobbying lawmakers on Capitol Hill, worried proposed changes by the Trump administration threaten the backbone of the federal preschool program

WASHINGTON -- Cassie Reed and her two young children had just moved from a domestic violence shelter into a third-floor apartment in Spokane, Washington, when she spotted a soon-to-open Head Start preschool on the building's ground floor.

Much of Reed's first three decades of life had been shaped by abuse and neglect: first, she says, at the hands of her biological mother, then in foster care and, when she became an adult, in a series of romantic relationships. She had lost custody of three older children a decade earlier, in part because she lacked stable housing. By March 2022, when she had finally landed an apartment in a transitional housing program, she had lost all faith in herself.
None of that was apparent this September, when she traveled to the nation's capital to tell members of Congress how her life changed when she enrolled her children in Head Start.

Reed says Head Start helped her heal from three decades of trauma and abuse. Staff connected her to job training, taught her how to be a better mother, helped her advocate for her son’s disability accommodations at his elementary school, and urged her to join the council that oversees Head Start across Spokane County, Washington. She was elected the council's president last year.
Head Start was, Reed says, “a warm blanket in a time where I constantly felt cold.”
That could be changing.

Last month, President Donald Trump’s administration proposed gutting Head Start regulations that spell out how programs must support families with financial, education or housing concerns. Many of the services now mandated would become optional.
Reed’s transformation was no fluke: Head Start’s services for low-income parents have been central to its model for decades.

“Being told that somebody believes in you and thinks you’re a good parent after so much loss — it didn’t feel real at first,” Reed said. “It took probably a year or two for me to be like, ‘OK, maybe I am. Maybe I just went through something that was really hard, but I was doing the best that I could.’”

Head Start, a six-decade-old preschool program, works to lift children and their families out of poverty. Its two-generation approach is rooted in the idea that improving caregivers' lives is as essential to a child's success as what happens in the classroom. Parents can also serve on committees that help set the direction of their kids' preschool.

“It’s always had that family connection,” said Loukisha Smart-Pennix of the YWCA of Metropolitan Chicago, which oversees several Head Start centers. “That’s been part and parcel of what Head Start was built on.”

Smart-Pennix said she's proof the approach works. When she was in the program as a preschooler in the 1970s, Head Start connected her mother with a factory job. Two decades later, when Smart-Pennix enrolled her son, the center employed her and pushed her to go to college. By the time her daughter was old enough to enroll, she earned too much to qualify. (Generally, families qualify for Head Start if their income is at or below the federal poverty line, currently $33,000 for a family of four.)

Under current regulations, Head Start asks parents to set goals — to return to school, to buy a home — and then helps them stay on track to achieve them. Parents have described how Head Start has helped them stay sober, finish school, pay off debt or simply keep the lights on. Operators are required to give hiring preferences to current and former Head Start parents, so many end up working for the program. Some eventually run their own preschools.

The Trump administration proposal would water down many of the family support regulations. Goal-setting with families would be optional, as would hiring preferences for Head Start parents. It would also scrap requirements for an open-door policy that gives parents liberal access to their child's classroom and cancel a mandate that staff visit homes and hold parent-teacher conferences at least twice per year. Programs would no longer be required to help parents navigate Medicaid, even as the government-funded health insurance program's rules are becoming more complex.

Head Start preschools would also have the option of eliminating parent committees, formal groups that weigh in on curriculum and programming. And policy councils, which have parent members, would see their authority weakened under the proposal.

Alex Adams, who leads the Department of Health and Human Services office overseeing Head Start, said the goal of the changes is to empower local leaders and to increase efficiency, enabling programs to serve up to 236,000 more children without additional funding.

“A one-size-fits-all mandate from Washington cannot fully account for the realities facing these 1,600 grantees” that operate Head Start preschools, Adams told reporters in August. “Federal mandates can certainly hinder local decision-making, drive up costs and limit the program’s reach.”

The Department of Health and Human Services said the proposal still recognizes the importance of parents in a child's learning, “but substantially reduces hyper-specificity for how to fulfill requirements, specifically around how programs must engage parents and families in education and child development services.”
“The proposal gives programs room to make thoughtful adjustments when local circumstances call for them,” the department said in a statement.

Head Start backers see the proposal not as a chance for flexibility but as another effort by the Trump administration to undermine the longstanding program. Days after Trump, a Republican, took office in early 2025, some Head Start programs temporarily closed their doors due to problems accessing their federal money. Later, a White House budget draft proposed eliminating funding for Head Start. The funding was restored after widespread backlash.
Adams emphasized programs wouldn't have to use the flexibility in the proposal if they want to continue operating as they have.
“It’s not a mandate," Adams told reporters. "The opportunity for these programs to make a different decision does not necessarily mean they must make a different decision.”

But advocates are skeptical. The administration's proposal eliminates requirements for small class sizes and scraps caseload limits for family support specialists. Centers instead would abide by their state's early learning regulations, which are often more lenient.

With more kids, fewer teachers, rising costs and no material increase in funding, advocates worry programs would be forced to dilute some of Head Start’s signature offerings. The Trump administration's own projections show that to add 236,000 slots for kids, Head Start centers would have to eliminate about 25,000 teacher jobs, increase class sizes and cut three-quarters of the staff who provide in-home education for new parents.
Reed says she worries the changes could mean fewer success stories like hers.
That's how she ended up in Washington, D.C. When Sen. Patty Murray, D-Wash., took a seat next to her, Reed grew nervous.
“Is it OK if I just read something from my phone?” she asked, shaking. Murray nodded.
She told the senator, a former preschool teacher, about the day she moved from a domestic violence shelter into transitional housing.
“At the bottom of our stairs was a Head Start center,” she said. “I had no idea how much it would change our lives.”

title: Trump's mail voting crackdown tests Postal Service leader who says he's 'not political'
summary: Before he was the top U_S_ Postal Service official, David Steiner criticized Donald Trump's leadership style after seeing him on "The Apprentice."
story: Before he was the top U_S_ Postal Service official, David Steiner criticized Donald Trump's leadership style after seeing him on "The Apprentice."

WASHINGTON -- Long before he was the top official at the U.S. Postal Service, David Steiner was a corporate executive surfing mid-oughts television when he came across Donald Trump on “The Apprentice.”
He was unimpressed.

“If that is leadership, if that's what we're telling people that our culture and our media portrays as leadership, we're screwed,” Steiner, then the CEO of Waste Management, said during a 2007 speech at the University of Arkansas Clinton School of Public Service. “If that's leadership, count me out.”
“And for God's sake,” he added to laughter, “if I have to get my hair to look like that, if I have to do that to be a leader, you can definitely count me out.”

Nearly two decades later, Trump has migrated from reality television to the presidency. And onetime detractors — Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Sen. Ted Cruz of Texas, for example — now loyally execute his agenda.
Trump's effort to use the Postal Service as a tool to reshape American elections is testing whether Steiner will follow a similar path.

When Trump signed an executive order restricting mail ballots this year, Steiner moved quickly to finalize a rule implementing the measure, arguing he had little choice. But after the U.S. Supreme Court rejected the effort, Steiner told The Associated Press that work had stopped on one of the plan's most controversial elements, a government portal for voter rolls.
He refused to endorse the Republican president's order as sound policy, saying he was focused on implementation and letting the courts ultimately decide the matter.
“I don't get to decide what rules that are put on us that I decide to accept or not accept,” he said. “We are an independent agency of the executive branch.”
The episode prompted fierce criticism of Steiner for allowing Trump to deploy an agency designed to be shielded from politics.

Jena Griswold, Colorado's Democratic secretary of state, called him a “Trump lackey.” Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar, a Democrat, recently asked Congress to deploy observers to ensure postal workers can scan envelopes holding mail ballots without disruption, saying the Trump administration "has attempted to weaponize federal agencies to interfere in our elections, and the leadership at USPS is going along with it.”

Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., accused Steiner of being a Trump “pawn” during a congressional hearing this summer. Dozens of congressional Democrats have pressed Steiner to reveal his interactions with the White House during the development of the mail ballot rule.

Some Republicans have joined in the criticism. Sen. Josh Hawley of Missouri, incensed by abandoned mail, called for Steiner's resignation and introduced legislation to block him from receiving a bonus.

During a lengthy interview, Steiner seemed surprised at points by his reception in Washington. He insisted he wasn't a “political person” and said he had no intention of stepping down despite the criticism. He dismissed heated congressional appearances as “theater” at odds with more substantive private interactions on Capitol Hill.

Steiner was chagrined, however, at the mention of his 2007 remarks on Trump, delivered well before he launched a political career. Steiner recalled speaking at the university but said he didn't remember his comments, acknowledging a tendency to be “flippant.”
“That's funny,” he said. “I don't recall it.”
The White House didn't respond to a request for comment on Steiner's remarks or his stewardship of the Postal Service.

The Postal Service dates to Benjamin Franklin, the first postmaster general, whose portrait and bust are displayed in Steiner's office overlooking the Washington Wharf. The agency has more than 630,000 employees, dwarfing many Cabinet departments.

While the quickest way to top jobs in Trump's Washington is often by writing big checks, the 66-year-old Steiner doesn’t appear to have followed that course. He has largely donated to Republicans but also gave to John Kerry’s Democratic presidential campaign in 2004. Unlike his predecessor as postmaster general, Louis DeJoy, Steiner was not a major GOP donor or Trump backer.

Born in Oakland, California, as one of eight children to a father who spent his career at Chevron, Steiner worked in corporate and securities law before moving to Waste Management in 2000. He became CEO in 2004 and ran the company for 12 years. He was also a longtime director at FedEx, where board chairman Brad Martin recalled him as “outcome oriented” and rarely political.
“He's going to follow the rules. He's going to follow the law,” Martin said. “I don't recall us ever talking politics.”
By the time a headhunter contacted Steiner about the postmaster general job, he was largely removed from daily corporate life and initially demurred.
“I talked to my wife, and we both agreed I was happily retired," he said.
He changed his mind, he said, during a visit to the beaches of Normandy, feeling a sense of civic duty.

Now at the Postal Service, he earns about $346,000 in annual salary along with a relocation bonus that amounts to half his salary, far less than the $17 million in compensation he earned during his final year at Waste Management. His current role is designed to exist one layer removed from the political process, reporting to a board of governors that is selected by the president and confirmed by the Senate.

He was hired in 2025 by a board that was made up of five members, three of whom were Democrats. All but one were appointed by President Joe Biden. That makeup could change as four Trump nominees — all Republicans — await Senate confirmation. Steiner can be fired only by the board.

Steiner said he first met Trump along with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick at the board's urging after he was already selected as postmaster general. Since then, he described a minimal relationship with the White House.
“We don't fly on the radar,” he said.
That is, until Trump revived his effort in March to crack down on mail voting. Steiner said he “wasn't in on the development piece” of the order and first saw it about a month before it was signed.
“They gave it to us to say, ‘Have your lawyers look at it, and how do you operationalize it?’” Steiner said.

The portal spurred a massive development effort inside the Postal Service while some states criticized it as federal overreach. A whistleblower report released by Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., argued the system was hastily built and riddled with errors, though Steiner said he was confident it could have been unveiled around Sept. 15.
“The heavy lifting was clearly, clearly the IT work,” Steiner said.
Though the Supreme Court dispensed with the rule, the dynamics for the Postal Service don't get easier.

The agency posted a $9 billion net loss last year, and Steiner has warned it could soon run out of cash unless Congress lifts a $15 billion borrowing cap. Political hurdles have prevented potential cost savings from cutting service or closing some post offices.

And while Trump's executive order won't take effect, the Postal Service will still play a critical role in this year's elections. There are mounting concerns that mail ballots could be rejected for late postmarks. Steiner encouraged voters to get their ballots in a week before the election to avoid problems.

The Postal Service is a rare corner of government still viewed favorably with more than half of Americans, 56%, saying it was doing an “excellent” or “good” job in a Gallup poll conducted last year. That could change if the agency is seen as increasingly political.
Steiner, however, said Americans will judge the Postal Service by their experience of it.

“What they care about is when they get that wedding invitation after the wedding or when they send a package and it disappears,” he said. “If we want to have the trust of the American public, let's be the best service provider. Everything else is noise.”

title: Kam Davis propels Liberty to 30-14 victory over Delaware in Conference USA opener
summary: Kam Davis rushed for 147 yards and two touchdowns to lead Liberty to a 30-14 victory over Delaware on in a Conference USA opener for both teams
story: Kam Davis rushed for 147 yards and two touchdowns to lead Liberty to a 30-14 victory over Delaware on in a Conference USA opener for both teams
NEWARK, Del. -- Kam Davis rushed for 147 yards and two touchdowns to lead Liberty to a 30-14 victory over Delaware on Friday night in a Conference USA opener for both teams.

Davis raced 56 yards for a touchdown on third-and-2 for a 13-0 lead midway through the second quarter. He added a 5-yard scoring run early in the fourth quarter to put the Flames (4-1) up 30-0. The junior totaled 123 yards on nine carries in the first half.
Deshawn Purdie completed 13 of 20 passes for 157 yards for Liberty.
Chase Reeves kicked two of his three field goals in the first quarter and the Flames never looked back.
Peyton Jones scored on a 3-yard run with 39 seconds left before halftime, capping a 12-play 98-yard drive as Liberty took a 20-0 advantage into halftime.
Sophomore EJ Archield Jr. had 137 yards on 10-for-19 passing for the Blue Hens (2-3) in his first collegiate start after Nick Minnicucci was injured last week in a 42-3 road loss to Virginia.

Blue Hens backups Braden Streeter and Tyler Bell had touchdown passes in the fourth quarter. Streeter connected with Donovan Lewis for a 58-yard score and Bell hit Matthew McKinley-Daniels for a 27-yard touchdown with 1:35 remaining.
Liberty: Hosts Sam Houston on Thursday.
Delaware: At Middle Tennessee on Oct. 13.

title: Blazing triple-digit heat bears down on Braves-Dodgers NLDS opener in Los Angeles
summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are hosting the Atlanta Braves in what is forecast to be the hottest postseason game at Dodger Stadium since 2017
story: The Los Angeles Dodgers are hosting the Atlanta Braves in what is forecast to be the hottest postseason game at Dodger Stadium since 2017
LOS ANGELES -- The Los Angeles Dodgers are hosting the Atlanta Braves in what is forecast to be the hottest postseason game at Dodger Stadium since 2017.

Shade was at a premium on Saturday for Game 1 of the National League Division Series, which began at 1 p.m. local time. The game-time temperature of 100 degrees was forecast to reach 101 degrees Fahrenheit (38 degrees Celsius), about 20 degrees warmer than the average for early October.

The highest game-time temperature ever recorded at Dodger Stadium is 103 degrees (39 degrees Celsius) twice. The first time was Oct. 24, 2017, for Game 1 of the World Series against Houston. It was equaled on Sept. 8, 2024, for a regular-season game against Cleveland.

The Braves seemingly were unfazed by the blazing sun, cloudless skies and rising thermometer while taking pre-game batting practice. The two-time defending World Series champion Dodgers? They stayed inside.
“Remember, we're from Atlanta,” Braves manager Walt Weiss said before the game. “It's not that big of a factor.”
Braves center fielder Lane Thomas added, "I feel like this is a little cooler 98 than Atlanta.”
Some of their fans agreed.

“It's hot, but it's not bad,” said Helen Greene of Valdosta, Georgia, who was sitting in the sun nine rows behind the visiting dugout with her long hair arrayed under a Braves cap. “In Atlanta, my hair would have been up by now.”
Greene and her husband, Chad, were hydrating with water.
“I'll have beer later,” she said, smiling.
Tickets for Game 1 were still available early Saturday. The lowest get-in price ranged from $56 to $61, depending on the secondary marketplace.
Fans still gathered in the outfield pavilions in hopes of catching a stray ball off the Braves' bats pre-game. But other seating areas were mostly empty 90 minutes before first pitch.
Christopher Hernández of Long Beach and his girlfriend sat in the sun behind the Dodgers dugout with giveaway towels covering their heads.

“We play sports and we know how it feels to be in the heat and we know how to beat the heat, too,” he said, showing off a blue plastic bottle with a fan attached to spritz water. “It's not as bad as people think it is.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts planned to keep an eye on his pitchers and catcher Will Smith, who wears a mask and padding behind the plate.
“It’s the same conditions for both teams,” the manager said, “and you’ve got to just stay hydrated and manage it.”
Braves reliever Brent Suter graduated from Harvard in 2012, having majored in environmental science and public policy.

“In the back of my mind, I’m like 100 degrees in October in L.A., that’s definitely not normal,” he said before the game. “Obviously super El Niño is a big thing to do with that. It’s going to be a challenge for both sides to stay hydrated, especially the position players.”

Short heat spells in October are normal for Los Angeles, but the prolonged extreme heat warning — forecast to last at least a week — is keeping temperatures 10 to 15 degrees above normal. The average high in Los Angeles in early October is 81 degrees (27 degrees Celsius).
“Just making sure everyone is hydrated and staying loose and getting electrolytes in us,” Suter said.

Emergency medical teams were in their usual spots around the stadium, staying alert for anticipated cases of heatstroke, dehydration, excessive sweating caused by heat exposure, and the more typical drunkenness.

The Dodgers encouraged fans to wear hats and sunscreen. They were allowed to bring in non-alcoholic drinks of one liter or less in factory-sealed plastic bottles. Empty refillable water bottles were also allowed. Bottle filling stations and water fountains are scattered around the stadium.

title: Panthers place Aleksander Barkov on long-term injured reserve with injury to left leg
summary: Florida center Aleksander Barkov has been placed on long-term injured reserve by the Panthers, meaning his injured left leg will keep him sidelined for at least the next 10 games and quite possibly beyond
story: Florida center Aleksander Barkov has been placed on long-term injured reserve by the Panthers, meaning his injured left leg will keep him sidelined for at least the next 10 games and quite possibly beyond

Florida center Aleksander Barkov has been placed on long-term injured reserve by the Panthers, meaning the injury to his left leg will keep him sidelined for at least the next 10 games and quite possibly beyond.

The Panthers have not revealed any details of Barkov's injury and it seems like the evaluation process to determine severity is ongoing. Barkov will see Panthers team physicians on Monday, coach Paul Maurice said.
Florida made a pair of roster additions after placing Barkov on the injured list Saturday, bringing up center Sam Lafferty and defenseman Alexander Petrovic.

Barkov was hurt midway through the second period of Florida's 4-3 overtime loss to the San Jose Sharks on Thursday night. He was jostling for the puck along the boards, got pushed by the Sharks' Darnell Nurse and awkwardly fell to the ice with his left leg at an unnatural angle. It appeared his knee buckled on the play.

Barkov remained down for a few moments, then got up and headed toward the tunnel leading to the Florida dressing room. He walked with a bit of a limp and appeared to angrily try to throw off his gloves as he moved toward the room.

Barkov — Florida's captain and a huge part of the Panthers' runs to Stanley Cup championships in 2024 and 2025 — missed the entire 2025-26 season with torn ligaments in his right knee. He went scoreless in his first two appearance of this season for Florida, which plays Sunday at Anaheim.

title: Mercer rolls up 658 yards offense on way to 54-3 victory over winless VMI
summary: Mercer quarterbacks Jaylen King, JP Pickles and Adrian Parker all threw touchdown passes and the Bears rolled past winless VMI 54-3 on Saturday
story: Mercer quarterbacks Jaylen King, JP Pickles and Adrian Parker all threw touchdown passes and the Bears rolled past winless VMI 54-3 on Saturday
LEXINGTON, Va. -- Mercer quarterbacks Jaylen King, JP Pickles and Adrian Parker all threw touchdown passes and the Bears rolled past winless VMI 54-3 on Saturday.
King was 14 of 23 in throwing for 202 of the Bears' 256 yards passing while Pickles ran for 66 yards including a score.

Zahmari Palode-Gary rushed for 130 yards on 10 carries with a touchdown and Karlise Price also scored in a 402-yard ground attack. Mercer (4-2, 1-1 Southern Conference) outgained the Keydets (0-6, 0-2) 658-102.
Pickles threw a 3-yard TD pass to Jackson Kostmayer to snap a 3-3 tie. Palode-Gary had a 64-yard TD run and King threw a 40-yard TD pass to Kel Calixte for a 27-3 halftime lead.
The Bears, ranked No. 23 in the Stats Perform poll, defeated VMI for the fifth straight time.

title: Austin Smotherman holds one-shot lead in Utah and goes after his first PGA Tour title
summary: Austin Smotherman had an answer every time someone caught up to him in the Bank of Utah Championship
story: Austin Smotherman had an answer every time someone caught up to him in the Bank of Utah Championship

IVINS, Utah -- Austin Smotherman responded with a string of birdies each time someone caught him Saturday in the Utah Championship, making one last birdie on the 18th hole for a 6-under 65 and a one-shot lead over Doug Ghim going into the final round.
At stake for Smotherman and Ghim is a chance at their first PGA Tour victory. Smotherman is making his 100th career start, Ghim his 192nd.
“I think it’s good pressure,” Smotherman said. “That’s what we work for. That’s the spot you want to be. Coming down, you kind of hold all the cards. I’m sure there’s going to be some energy.”
Smotherman three-putted from just outside 30 feet on the the par-4 10th, a bogey that enabled Kevin Streelman to tie him for the lead. Smotherman then birdied three of the next four holes.

Then it was Ghim's turn. He holed an 8-foot birdie on the par-3 17th and birdied the par-5 closing hole at Black Desert Resort with a nifty pitch to 3 feet. Both times the birdie gave him a share of the lead. Both times, Smotherman in the final group behind him matched birdies.
The last birdie was a 12-footer that put Smotherman at 23-under 190. His score to par already matches the 72-hole record at Black Desert, in its third year hosting the tournament.

It was the third straight round for at least one player posting a 62, this time from Johnny Keefer, who had to settle for a par when he drove into the lava area left of the par-5 ninth and had to pitch out sideways.

So much of the focus on the FedEx Cup Fall Series is on the top 100 players who secure full PGA Tour cards for 2027. But there's a huge perk for the winners of the eight tournaments — they get a two-year exemption, and that includes starting 2028 on the top-tier Championship Series.

Streelman is the only player from the top five on the leaderboard to have won on the PGA Tour, and the stakes are high for him, too. Streelman had a major medical exemption expire and now is battling to regain his card.

He was tied with Smotherman until a four-shot swing on the 13th hole. Smotherman made a birdie, while Streelman drove into the water off the tee and had to hit again, then found a bunker with his approach and failed to get up-and-down, making triple bogey.
Streelman birdied two of his last three holes and was five shots behind, along with Trace Crowe and Ben James, each with a 64.

Ghim fell back with his first bogey of the tournament on the par-5 ninth. He hit a pedestrian drive that left him 279 yards away. He went for the green and sailed right into lava rocks. He took the stroke-and-distance penalty, laid up, and holed a 13-foot putt for bogey to limit the damage.
“My first bogey of the week, but it didn't feel like one,” Ghim said.
He answered with six birdies on the back nine to get back in the game, giving him a good chance to finally get that first PGA Tour title.

“It’s what we come here to do — 191 times before I wanted to win, and I get another opportunity to do it tomorrow,” Ghim said. “It would be a dream come true. But at the same time, there’s a lot of really good players with a lot to play for. Just going to go out there and try to execute the best that I can and hopefully see where that puts me.”

title: Jackson Arnold accounts for 5 TDs as UNLV beats California 39-31
summary: Jackson Arnold passed and ran for 287 yards and five touchdowns to lead UNLV to a 39-31 victory over California on Saturday
story: Jackson Arnold passed and ran for 287 yards and five touchdowns to lead UNLV to a 39-31 victory over California on Saturday
LAS VEGAS -- Jackson Arnold passed and ran for 287 yards and five touchdowns to lead UNLV to a 39-31 victory over short-handed California on Saturday.

The Rebels (3-2) led 24-7 at halftime before Cal (2-3) rallied to go in front 25-24 early in the fourth quarter. Then Arnold completed a 10-yard pass to Keyan Burnett with 9:31 left and ran it in himself from 2 yards with 3:24 remaining.
Arnold passed for 177 yards and three touchdowns and rushed for 110 yards and two touchdowns.

Cal entered the game without leading rusher Adam Mohammed because of an injured knee, and then lost safety Kingston Lopa — whose five interceptions led the nation — to an upper-body injury less than three minutes into the first quarter. Quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele went out late in the first half and didn't return.
Jackson Brousseau replaced Sagapolutele and completed 19 of 32 passes for 200 yards and two touchdowns.

Sagapolutele threw 27 passes in the first two quarters as the Golden Bears went pass heavy. He completed 19 of them for 195 yards, including a 91-yarder to tight end Taimane Purcell. That touchdown — three-and-a-half minutes in — gave Cal a 7-0 lead before UNLV answered with a series of big plays of its own.

Arnold connected with Kayden McGee for a 70-yard touchdown, he then kept it himself for a 55-yard touchdown run in the second quarter and later tossed a 36-yard score to Taz Reddicks for a 24-7 halftime lead.
Cal wasn't done, however, coming all the way back to go in front by a point early in the fourth, forcing the Rebels to provide their own answer.

Cal: The Bears often failed to take advantage of opportunities. An interception return put them well into UNLV territory in the first quarter, but Sagapolutele gave it right back with a pick of his own. The Bears tried a surprise onside kick to open the second half, but failed to score. And then there was a fumbled kickoff recovery late in the third quarter that turned into three points rather than seven.
UNLV: The Rebels showed a mental fortitude after blowing a 17-point halftime lead and immediately scored twice after Cal went in front.
Cal: Hosts Virginia Tech next Saturday in its third ACC game.
UNLV: Returns to Mountain West play next Saturday by hosting conference newcomer North Dakota State.

title: Cameran Brown's school-record 6 touchdown passes lead Georgia State to 42-10 rout of Old Dominion
summary: Cameran Brown threw a school-record six touchdown passes and Georgia State flew past Old Dominion 42-10
story: Cameran Brown threw a school-record six touchdown passes and Georgia State flew past Old Dominion 42-10
ATLANTA -- Cameran Brown threw a school-record six touchdown passes and Georgia State flew past Old Dominion 42-10 on Saturday.

The Panthers (4-1) won their Sun Belt opener in convincing fashion, outgaining the Monarchs 470-142 in total yards and at one point scoring six touchdowns on eight possessions — all on throws by Brown. The streak was interrupted only by a punt and the end of the second quarter.
Brown's six touchdowns came on only 14 completions. He was 14-for-20 for 284 yards with all six touchdowns coming in the first three quarters before he gave way to Ayden Pereira.

Five players caught TD passes for the Panthers, with Rodshaun Dorsey grabbing two. Qwantavius Wiggins' 87 yards led Georgia State's 187 yards on the ground. Linebacker Xavier Esqillion had three of Georgia State's seven sacks.
Three Old Dominion quarterbacks combined for 79 yards on 13 of 28 passing and the Monarchs (1-4, 0-2) had 63 yards rushing.
Old Dominion: at Appalachian State next Saturday
Georgia State: at James Madison on Oct. 17

title: Nick Schmaltz scores twice, reaches 500 points as Mammoth beat Blue Jackets 4-1
summary: Nick Schmaltz had two goals and the Utah Mammoth scored three times on the power play to beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 4-1 on Saturday night for its second straight victory to open the season
story: Nick Schmaltz had two goals and the Utah Mammoth scored three times on the power play to beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 4-1 on Saturday night for its second straight victory to open the season

COLUMBUS, Ohio -- Nick Schmaltz had two goals and the Utah Mammoth scored three times on the power play to beat the Columbus Blue Jackets 4-1 on Saturday night for its second straight victory to open the season.
Mikhail Sergachev and Dylan Guenther each scored power-play goals. Sergachev added an assist and Guenther and Logan Cooley each had two assists. Sebastian Cossa stopped 15 shots in his Utah debut.
Clayton Keller had two assists to reach 600 NHL career points. He has two goals and 15 assists for 17 points in 17 career games against the Blue Jackets and four assists this season.
Kent Johnson scored for Columbus, and Jet Greaves stopped 21 shots. Matthew Knies had an assist, giving him four points in his first two games with the Blue Jackets.
Sergachev put Utah ahead with a power-play goal from near the blue line at 11:55 of the first period. Schmaltz doubled the lead less than five minutes later.
Johnson scored on a breakaway 1:30 into the second period to make it 2-1 before Guenther scored on the power play at 5:59 of the third for his third power-play goal in Utah’s first two games.
Schmaltz made it 4-1 with a power-play goal at 14:13 for his 500th NHL point.
The game opened a five-game road trip for Utah and was the first half of a back-to-back.
Mammoth: At the New York Rangers on Sunday night.
Blue Jackets: Hosts the Pittsburgh on Friday night.

title: McDavid has a goal and an assist as the Oilers beat the Kraken 3-1
summary: Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist to give him nine points through three games as the Edmonton Oilers beat the Seattle Kraken 3-1 on Saturday night
story: Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist to give him nine points through three games as the Edmonton Oilers beat the Seattle Kraken 3-1 on Saturday night
EDMONTON, Alberta -- Connor McDavid had a goal and an assist to give him nine points through three games as the Edmonton Oilers beat the Seattle Kraken 3-1 on Saturday night.
Owen Michaels and Leon Draisaitl also scored for the Oilers (2-0-1). Devon Levi made 19 stops to earn the win in the Oilers’ net.
Bobby McMann had the lone goal for the Kraken (1-1-0). Philipp Grubauer recorded 22 saves for Seattle.
After McMann made it a 1-1 game 9:06 into the second period, it was Draisaitl who eventually broke the deadlock.
Draisaitl scored with 2:27 left in regulation, with McDavid adding an empty-netter with 1:05 remaining.
Edmonton has gone 15-4-1 against the Kraken, including winning eight of nine meetings at home.

title: Start delayed again as cars struggle in wet conditions ahead of F1's Bahrain GP in Malaysia
summary: The start has been delayed again after several cars seemed to experience technical problems on the formation lap following heavy rain as Formula 1 holds its Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia
story: The start has been delayed again after several cars seemed to experience technical problems on the formation lap following heavy rain as Formula 1 holds its Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

SEPANG, Malaysia -- The start has been delayed again after several cars seemed to experience technical problems on the formation lap following heavy rain as Formula 1 holds its Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

Heavy rain delayed the formation lap by 40 minutes and when it eventually got under way, Lewis Hamilton went slowly and briefly stopped on track before he got going again. Soon after, the start procedure was suspended.
“I’m pressing the throttle and nothing’s happening," he told the Ferrari team, who said they were investigating a software problem.
Hamilton was due to start second on the grid behind Max Verstappen, who also complained to the Red Bull team of acceleration issues.
This is due to be the first wet-weather race for F1 in 2026. This year's cars depend heavily on complex algorithms to use their electrical hybrid power.
The race was relocated because of the Iran war, becoming F1's first event at the Sepang circuit in Malaysia since 2017.

title: Sydney Roosters wins NRL Grand Final with 19-18 win against Newcastle Knights
summary: The Sydney Roosters rallied from 12-0 down to win the NRL Grand Final, beating the Newcastle Knights 19-18
story: The Sydney Roosters rallied from 12-0 down to win the NRL Grand Final, beating the Newcastle Knights 19-18
SYDNEY -- The Sydney Roosters rallied from 12-0 down to win the NRL Grand Final, beating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 on Sunday.
In front of a crowd of 80,814 at Sydney's Accor Stadium, the Roosters sealed victory by the finest of margins with Daly Cherry-Evans' 70th-minute field goal proving decisive.
The Knights had raced to an early lead with tries from Francis Manuleleua and Kalyn Ponga and conversions by Sandon Smith.
But the Roosters powered back with tries from Mark Nawaqanitawase either side of another from Billy Smith and two conversions by Sam Walker.
Cherry-Evans' crucial kick was followed by a try from Greg Marzhew for the Knights in the closing stages to set up a tense finish.

“I'm so proud of this team. What a game,” Roosters captain James Tedesco said. “It felt like we had them on the ropes, but they kept coming back. They've got so many great attacking players, the game could have gone either way.”
On Saturday, a vehicle drove into a crowd standing on a road to cheer on the Knights team as it left Newcastle on its way to Sydney, injuring 10 people, including several children.
Earlier Sunday, the Sydney Roosters won the women’s competition with a 30-6 victory over the defending champion Brisbane Broncos to complete a perfect season of 13 consecutive wins.

title: Maye overcomes his two turnovers with 3 TD passes in Patriots' 29-26 win over Bills
summary: Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, including Efton Chism’s one-handed catch with 1:50 remaining, and the New England Patriots defeated the Buffalo Bills 29-26
story: Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, including Efton Chism’s one-handed catch with 1:50 remaining, and the New England Patriots defeated the Buffalo Bills 29-26
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Drake Maye threw three touchdown passes, including Efton Chism’s one-handed catch with 1:50 remaining, and the New England Patriots defeated the Buffalo Bills 29-26 on Sunday.
Romeo Doubs had touchdown catches of 2 and 14 yards, and Rhamondre Stevenson scored on a 1-yard run.
Though Maye’s turnover troubles continued with an interception and a lost fumble in the first half, the third-year starter was sharp in the final minutes after New England fell behind 26-21.

Maye’s 23-yard TD pass to Chism came on third-and-5, with the receiver bringing in the ball with his right hand and maintaining control in the end zone. Maye then hit Stevenson for the 2-point conversion.

Despite having a minute left and the ball at their 40, Josh Allen turned overly aggressive. On second-and-6, he spun out of Dre'Mont Jones' sack attempt, stepped up in the pocket and went deep only to have his underthrown pass intended for Josh Palmer intercepted by Craig Woodson.
Taking over at the Patriots 19, Maye put the finishing touches on the win by rolling to his right and lobbing a 12-yard pass to Hunter Henry in allowing the Patriots to run out the clock.
The Patriots improved to 2-2 and for once put aside questions about a sputtering and turnover-prone offense.
The Bills, meantime, dropped to 3-1 in Buffalo's first loss at its new Highmark Stadium, and first under new coach Joe Brady.

Maye finished 22 of 37 for 269 yards in overcoming the criticism he’s faced in opening the season by combining for six interceptions and a lost fumble in his first three starts. The lost fumble, recovered by the Buffalo at its 30, was on Maye, who lost the ball as Bills tackle Ed Oliver shoved an offensive lineman into him.
The interception, however, was on Doubs, who made the catch and in the process spun around and lost control of the ball, which sailed into the hands of cornerback Dee Alford.
The Bills had their sloppy moments, too, a week after committing five turnovers in a 24-16 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

Receiver Khalil Shakir lost a fumble, in addition to Allen’s interception — his third of the season. Allen finished 23 of 33 for 253 yards, including a 34-yard go-ahead touchdown to Keon Coleman with 4:27 remaining. The touchdown put Buffalo up 26-21, but the 2-point conversion attempt failed when Palmer never looked for Allen’s pass directed his way.
Allen also scored on a 2-yard run, while James Cook scored on an 8-yard run.
The Bills were limited to 340 total yards and 19 first downs, both season lows, and resembled nothing like the high-powered unit that opened the season combining for 855 yards and 77 points.

The outing was a breakthrough for the Patriots’ slumbering offense, which posted season highs with 405 yards and 26 first downs. New England’s defense also rallied in containing the Bills despite missing its top cornerback Christian Gonzalez and starting defensive tackle Christian Barmore because of shoulder injuries.

Allen’s 2-yard touchdown run to tie the game at 14 with one minute left in the first half was his 88th career from scrimmage (rushing/receiving) to break the team record held by Hall of Famers Thurman Thomas and Andre Reed. It was also Allen’s 86th TD rushing, moving him into a tie with Priest Holmes for 16th place on the NFL's career list.
Patriots: WR Mack Hollins hurt his calf.

Bills: WR DJ Moore did not return after hurting his shoulder attempting to make a diving catch in the second quarter. DT Ed Oliver left in the third quarter with a knee injury. And a secondary already missing Christian Benford (toe), lost Dee Alford to an ankle injury in the second half.
Patriots: host the Las Vegas on Sunday.
Bills: at the Los Angeles Rams on "Monday Night Football" on Oct. 12

title: New York Liberty face the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals
summary: Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty have been in this spot often in the last few seasons
story: Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty have been in this spot often in the last few seasons
NEW YORK -- Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty have been in this spot often in the last few seasons.
New York will be making its third appearance in the semifinals of the WNBA playoffs in the past four years when the Liberty play the Atlanta Dream on Sunday in Game 1 of the best-of-five series.
“Experience in the playoffs definitely matters,” Stewart said Friday before practice. “There’s so many things (during a longer series) that you have to stay focused on the end goal."
That end goal would be reaching the WNBA Finals and trying to win a second title in three seasons.

“With this group, for the majority of us, (we’ve) been in this type of series, where it’s not getting too high or too low is the huge important part,” Stewart said. “And what we did in the first round is great — we’re happy to be here — but that wasn’t a goal for our season to get out of the first round.”
New York was dominant in the first round while sweeping the Minnesota Lynx, becoming the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in the league’s 30-year history.

“The approach that we’re having in these playoffs is pretty much where you want to be,” Stewart added. “We’re the ones that are staying poised, staying under control at all times. But we’re gonna be aggressive for the full 40 minutes, and if you want something, you’re gonna have to go through us to get it."

Atlanta is the newcomer to this round, advancing this far for the first time since 2018. Aware of the team's lack of playoff experience other than Jordin Canada, Dream GM Dan Padover went out and got DeWanna Bonner as a free agent in late August. Bonner has played 100 games in the playoffs, the most in league history.
She joined a stacked lineup that includes Rhyne Howard, Allisha Gray and Angel Reese. That group lifted the Dream to their first playoff win since 2016 when they swept the Washington Mystics.

“I think the pace that they were playing with was really good,” Liberty coach Chris DeMarco said. "I think (Bonner) brought a lot of veteran leadership to them, a lot of timely scoring to really settle them into games. I think Howard and Gray are just two really good — or great guards that we have to slow down. When the game gets tough, they kind of put their heads down and kind of take over that scoring.”

The Atlanta Dream had one of the best defenses in the league this year, anchored by the WNBA Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese. Atlanta led the league in steals per game (9.1), which it converted to 18.1 points per game. The Dream raised that in the playoffs, scoring 27 points off miscues in their Game 1 win over Washington and getting 23 more in the clincher.
They are very active getting into passing lanes, which makes scoring in transition difficult.

The two teams met in the final two games of the regular season with the No. 4 seed on the line, and the Dream won both those contests. Stewart sat out the second game to get some rest heading into the playoffs. Neither team puts much stock in the value of those two games, other than they provided fresh film to both sides from late in the season.

The Dream will play the first two games of the semifinals in State Farm Arena, home of the Atlanta Hawks. Atlanta played six regular-season games at the arena, which seats more than 17,000 fans. The Dream's usual home, the Gateway Center Arena, holds about 3,500. Atlanta played Game 1 of its series against the Mystics at State Farm Arena. If the Dream win in the semifinals, it's unclear what they'll do for the Finals since singer Sombr is performing there the night of Game 3 and the Hawks have their home opener the same evening as Game 4.

title: Yoder and Morgan power Lehigh past Fordham 34-0
summary: Luke Yoder rushed for 171 yards and a touchdown and Derek Morgan threw three touchdown passes as Lehigh shut out Fordham 34-0 on Saturday
story: Luke Yoder rushed for 171 yards and a touchdown and Derek Morgan threw three touchdown passes as Lehigh shut out Fordham 34-0 on Saturday
BETHLEHEM, Pa. -- Luke Yoder rushed for 171 yards and a touchdown and Derek Morgan threw three touchdown passes as Lehigh shut out Fordham 34-0 on Saturday.
The Mountain Hawks (6-0, 4-0 Patriot), ranked No. 6 in the Stats Perform poll, scored 31 points in the second quarter and forced five turnovers.
Morgan opened the scoring with a 30-yard touchdown pass to Anthony Feaster before connecting with Aiden Schomp for a 10-yard score to make it 14-0.

Lehigh recovered a Fordham fumble on the ensuing kickoff late in the half, and Yoder scored on a 10-yard run with 44 seconds remaining. Morgan then hit Feaster for a 29-yard touchdown with 19 seconds left, and Connor Poole added a 26-yard field goal as time expired to make it 31-0.
Feaster finished with three catches for 67 yards and two touchdowns. Morgan completed 10 of 20 passes for 152 yards without an interception.
Lehigh held Fordham (1-5, 1-2 Patriot) to 42 yards rushing and intercepted Gunnar Smith three times. Nick Peltekian, William Parton and Ignatious Williams each had an interception.
Smith threw for 190 yards and three interceptions.

title: Keelon Russell accounts for 4 TDs as No. 7 Alabama routs No. 16 Mississippi State 56-23
summary: Keelon Russell passed for 285 yards and three touchdowns to go with a rushing score, and No. 7 Alabama routed 16th-ranked Mississippi State 56-23 in a matchup of previously unbeaten teams
story: Keelon Russell passed for 285 yards and three touchdowns to go with a rushing score, and No. 7 Alabama routed 16th-ranked Mississippi State 56-23 in a matchup of previously unbeaten teams

STARKVILLE, Miss. -- Keelon Russell passed for 285 yards and three touchdowns to go with a rushing score, and No. 7 Alabama routed 16th-ranked Mississippi State 56-23 on Saturday in a matchup of previously unbeaten teams.

“Just going out there, just having fun, understanding the assignment, doing me, playing my game," said the 19-year-old Russell, who turned the ball over three times at Kentucky in his first Southeastern Conference road game but committed none against the Bulldogs.
“You make your mistakes and you learn from it,” Russell said. "And I feel like that’s what I’m doing.”

Trae'shawn Brown ran for two touchdowns, Rico Scott caught two TD passes and Dijon Lee Jr. returned an interception 30 yards for a score during a game that saw Alabama (5-0, 3-0 SEC) reinforce its credentials as contenders.
Alabama outgained Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1) 179-18 in yards rushing in its 17th straight victory in the series — the last seven by 23 or more points.

The game featured two of college football's most dynamic quarterbacks this season, but the mobility of the Bulldogs' Kamario Taylor appeared limited by an ankle injury last week and he struggled Saturday. His early fumble and two interceptions set up Alabama touchdown drives.

“It’s pretty obvious that he wasn’t able to do anything with his legs,” Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby said. “So, him not being able to do some of those things, it changes it. It makes it harder.”
Taylor was sacked five times and pulled from the game with the Bulldogs down by 26 early in the fourth quarter.
“He did look kind of iffy getting out of the pocket and stuff and we knew that,” Alabama linebacker Caleb Woodson. “So, we knew we had a better chance to contain him.”
Leading Bulldogs receiver Anthony Evans III had 12 catches for 166 yards and two touchdowns, one of his team's few bright spots.
What was widely seen as the biggest game at Davis Wade Stadium since Dak Prescott starred at QB for the Bulldogs more than a decade ago started poorly for Mississippi State.
Taylor's first two turnovers put the Bulldogs in a 14-0 hole less than seven minutes into the first quarter.
He fumbled five plays into the opening possession when the ball slipped from his throwing hand on an apparent pump fake near midfield and Alabama's London Simmons recovered.
That led to Ryan Coleman-Williams' 15-yard touchdown on Russell's short pass to the right flat. Taylor's next pass resulted in Lee's pick-6.
Taylor finished with 258 yards and three TDs passing, including an 11-yard score to Zion Riggins that pulled the Bulldogs to 21-14 in the second quarter.
But Alabama responded again with Brown's 7-yard scoring run, capping an 88-yard drive highlighted by Russell's third-down completions of 50 yards to Lotzeir Brooks and 22 yards to Coleman-Williams.
“He moves around, throws a shot and they pick up a huge first down," Lebby said. “He’s really accurate, got great anticipation and you continue to see him make big plays with his feet.”
Brooks finished with four catches for 96 yards.

Alabama: Russell continued to improve his Heisman Trophy credentials by playing with composure amid the usual din of ringing cowbells at Mississippi State. He avoided turnovers and had several clutch completions on third down — including connections of 39 and 50 yards, and his touchdown pass to Scott.

“Not really worrying about the Heisman right now. Accolades and stuff will come," Russell said. “I don’t want to spoil myself too much about what I can get and rather (focus on) what am I going to do to make myself better.”

Mississippi State: Top running back Fluff Bothwell, who entered the game nursing a lower-body injury, carried the ball only once for 1 yard on the Bulldogs' opening series and watched the second half with a boot on his left foot. Bothwell had entered the game with 402 yards and three TDs rushing. Lebby did not provide specifics on the injury after the game.
Alabama: Hosts No. 2 Georgia next Saturday.
Mississippi State: Has a bye before visiting No. 11 LSU on Oct. 17.
This story has been updated to correct that Russell had three turnovers, not three interceptions, at Kentucky.

title: Nathan Hayes runs for 2 TDs, Bison defense stellar in 28-0 win over Wyoming
summary: Nathan Hayes ran for two touchdowns and North Dakota State’s defense smothered Wyoming in a 28-0 win on Saturday in the Bison’s first-ever Mountain West Conference home game
story: Nathan Hayes ran for two touchdowns and North Dakota State’s defense smothered Wyoming in a 28-0 win on Saturday in the Bison’s first-ever Mountain West Conference home game
FARGO, N.D. -- Nathan Hayes ran for two touchdowns and North Dakota State's defense smothered Wyoming in a 28-0 win on Saturday in the Bison's first-ever Mountain West Conference home game.

On the game's first play from scrimmage, Donovan Woolen intercepted Wyoming's Tyler Hughes to set up the Bison (5-0, 2-0) at the Wyoming 19-yard line, leading to Hayes' 8-yard TD scramble. Hayes made it 14-0 with a 14-yard run around the right end with a Drew Klein field goal extending the lead to 17-0 by halftime.
Klein added another field goal and DJ Scott scored from a yard out in the second half.
The Cowboys (2-3, 1-1) managed just 162 yards offense. Their best chance to score came after a fumble put them at the Bison 26-yard line but that possession ended on downs at the 5.
The shutout was the second for the Bison this season after blanking Fordham 38-0 on Sept. 5. The last time the Cowboys were shut out came in 2022 — a 30-0 loss to Fresno State.
The two programs played the first game in the newly created Battle of the Basins, a traveling trophy to go to the winner annually.

title: Camden Coleman, George Pettaway lead unbeaten James Madison to 45-17 romp over Marshall
summary: Camden Coleman threw three touchdown passes, and George Pettaway rushed for two scores and a career-high 206 yards to lead unbeaten James Madison to a 45-17 victory over Marshall in the Thundering Herd’s Sun Belt Conference opener
story: Camden Coleman threw three touchdown passes, and George Pettaway rushed for two scores and a career-high 206 yards to lead unbeaten James Madison to a 45-17 victory over Marshall in the Thundering Herd’s Sun Belt Conference opener

HARRISONBURG, Va. -- Camden Coleman threw three touchdown passes, and George Pettaway rushed for two scores and a career-high 206 yards to lead unbeaten James Madison to a 45-17 victory over Marshall on Saturday in the Thundering Herd's Sun Belt Conference opener.

Coleman completed 21 of 32 passes for 263 yards for James Madison (5-0, 2-0), which fell behind for the first time this season before scoring 28 straight in the final 12 minutes of the second quarter.
Pettaway scored on runs of 73 and 33 yards between a pair of touchdown passes from Coleman as the Dukes turned a four-point deficit into a 38-14 halftime lead.
Carlos Del Rio-Wilson had a 3-yard scoring toss to Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw on Marshall's first possession for a 7-0 lead.
Coleman connected with Corey Scott for a 53-yard touchdown to tie it after Michael Scott's 45-yard kickoff return set the Dukes up at their own 45-yard line.

TJ Lester's 1-yard scoring run gave Marshall a 14-10 lead early in the second quarter, but Coleman and Corey Scott teamed up for a 12-yard touchdown and the Dukes never trailed again. Corey Scott finished with five receptions for 104 yards.
Pettaway followed with his long touchdown runs, and Coleman hit Noah Grevious for a 20-yard score and a big lead at halftime after scoring on six straight possessions.
Nick Herman had a 3-yard touchdown run in the final minute for the Dukes.
Del Rio-Wilson totaled 221 yards on 21-for-37 passing for Marshall (3-2). He and backup Zion Turner both had a pass picked off by DJ Kelly.
Marshall junior linebacker Chason Clark was injured near the end of the third quarter and taken off the field on a stretcher.
Marshall: Hosts Coastal Carolina on Saturday.

title: Sam Leavitt leads LSU to 63-14 victory over McNeese State
summary: LSU dominated McNeese State 63-14, with Sam Leavitt throwing for 173 yards and three touchdowns
story: LSU dominated McNeese State 63-14, with Sam Leavitt throwing for 173 yards and three touchdowns
BATON ROUGE, La. -- Sam Leavitt threw for 173 yards and three touchdowns and No. 11 LSU beat McNeese State 63-14 on Saturday night.

Harlem Berry ran for 125 yards and a touchdown and Stacy Gage added 110 yards and two touchdowns on the ground, as the Tigers rolled to 731 yards of total offense against their Football Championship Subdivision foe — the second-most in one game in school history and the most since 2023. The 101 offensive plays run by LSU is a school record.

“Outside of a few plays late I thought our guys played really well,” LSU head coach Lane Kiffin said. “I know you are supposed to win these games big, but it doesn’t always happen. I thought our guys responded well particularly coming out of the locker room and played well in the third quarter. It was good to see a lot of guys make plays.

“A lot of snaps for guys. The goal was to get (that up) to evaluate those guys because they are going to need to play with the injuries we have down the stretch. We have seven consecutive conference games in a row. 101 plays is a lot of snaps for the backups to get in there and do some things.”

The defense got things started for LSU (4-1) when Tamarcus Cooley intercepted Jake Strong on McNeese State’s first possession. Nine plays later, Dilin Jones scored from a yard out to give the Tigers a 7-0 lead.

Three consecutive three-and-outs by the Tigers defense helped LSU put the game out of reach early in the second quarter. Leavitt had a 1-yard touchdown pass to Roman Mothershed and a 6-yard touchdown pass to Corey Barber Jr. sandwiched around a 3-yard touchdown run by Landen Clark to make it 28-0.
Barber finished the game with six catches for 76 yards and a pair of touchdowns.
Leavitt completed 18 of 23 passes.
LSU dominated the first half, outgaining the Cowboys (2-4) 347-31. McNeese State’s offense crossed midfield only once during the first half.
Freshman defensive tackle Deuce Geralds even got in on the scoring for the Tigers, scoring from a yard out on a direct snap on LSU’s first possession of the second half to make it 42-0.

“I asked our historian just before we walked in if anyone had ever had a sack and an offensive touchdown,” Kiffin said. “He said yes, Booger (Anthony McFarland) had done it against Florida (in 1995). But he had half a sack and a touchdown. I just actually called Booger to confirm that and he said Deuce has the record now.”
Gage scored on runs of 46 and 39 yards in the second half.

The Cowboys got on the board with under five minutes to go in the third quarter on a 43-yard touchdown pass from backup quarterback Brady Barrier to Jamaal Levi to make it 49-7. He added a 64-yard touchdown run on the ensuing possession to make it 49-14.

McNeese State: The Cowboys weren’t expected to contend in the game against the Tigers and it was evident from the opening possession. Levi’s two touchdowns did give McNeese State its most points scored in the brief three-game history of the series, surpassing the 10 points they scored in 2010.

LSU: Still not 100% because of a nagging hamstring injury, Leavitt was effective in the pocket, completing 10 of his first 12 passes. The Tigers also got plenty of work for backup quarterback Clark, who played a majority of the third quarter.
McNeese State travels to Northwestern State on Oct. 17.
LSU travels to Kentucky next Saturday.

title: No. 18 USC rallies past Washington 25-21 with Stewart's fumble return TD, more big defensive plays
summary: No. 18 Southern California rallied from a double-digit deficit in the second half for a 25-21 victory over Washington
story: No. 18 Southern California rallied from a double-digit deficit in the second half for a 25-21 victory over Washington

LOS ANGELES -- Jahkeem Stewart returned a fumble 48 yards for the go-ahead touchdown, and No. 18 Southern California overcame a double-digit deficit in the second half for a 25-21 victory over Washington on Saturday night.

Jayden Maiava passed for 245 yards and hit Tanook Hines for a second-half score while the Trojans (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten) surged back with the game's final 15 points for their first victory over the Huskies (3-2, 0-2) since 2016.

Demond Williams Jr. passed for 198 yards and led Washington on a late drive from its 5 to the USC 12, converting two fourth downs and a third-and-11 along the way. But after Kameryn Crawford sacked Williams on third down, Williams' pass into double coverage in the end zone fell incomplete with 39 seconds left.
The win eases some of the pressure on coach Lincoln Riley and the Trojans, who improved sharply on defense after last week's dispiriting home loss to Oregon.

Clear chants of “Fire Lincoln! Fire Lincoln!” could be heard from the student section in the second half while the Trojans fell behind 21-10, but coordinator Gary Patterson's defense didn't allow any more points by the depleted Huskies, who have lost two straight by a combined seven points.

That USC defense turned the game around late in the third quarter when Stewart — the 295-pound defensive tackle nicknamed Thanos — picked up Williams’ fumble in a collapsing pocket and rumbled downfield for his first score.
Receiver Dezmen Roebuck threw a touchdown pass to Baron Naone for Washington’s first points.

Washington went up 14-10 shortly before halftime with an 80-yard drive ending in Kade Eldridge's TD dive. After USC had two drives sabotaged by unsportsmanlike conduct penalties on either side of halftime, Decker DeGraaf took a short pass for a 42-yard score when multiple Trojans failed to push him out of bounds.
But Hines ripped a 10-yard TD pass away from a Washington defensive back later in the third before the Trojans went ahead on Stewart's TD.
USC linebacker Desman Stephens sat out under suspension after his ejection last week for a late hit on Ducks quarterback Dante Moore. Ta'Mere Robinson took Stephens' starting spot.

Washington: Two heartbreaking losses put the brakes on the Huskies' hopes of entering the AP Top 25, but coach Jedd Fisch is getting decent efforts out of a roster with injury problems. Their remaining October schedule is fairly friendly to a resurgence if the defense can get back on track.

USC: The defense responded smartly to a poor September, holding the Huskies to 123 yards in the first half before making enough big plays to win it late. A series of crushing penalties prevented the Trojans from running away, but Riley will take any win at this point in his tumultuous tenure.

title: Madsen, No. 22 Boise State beat Utah State 37-18 in the teams' inaugural Pac-12 game
summary: Maddux Madsen was 17-of-21 passing for 244 yards and two touchdowns, Dylan Riley added two rushing touchdowns, and No. 22 Boise State beat Utah State 37-18 in the inaugural game as a member of the Pac-12 Conference for both teams
story: Maddux Madsen was 17-of-21 passing for 244 yards and two touchdowns, Dylan Riley added two rushing touchdowns, and No. 22 Boise State beat Utah State 37-18 in the inaugural game as a member of the Pac-12 Conference for both teams

BOISE, Idaho -- Maddux Madsen was 17-of-21 passing for 244 yards and two touchdowns, Dylan Riley added two rushing touchdowns and No. 22 Boise State beat Utah State 37-18 on Saturday in the inaugural game as a member of the Pac-12 Conference for both teams.
Boise State (4-1) has won four in a row since a 34-27 loss to then-No. 2 Oregon in the season opener and made its season debut in the AP Top 25.

The Broncos have won 11 straight against Utah State and 12 in a row at home against the Aggies. Boise State leads the series 26-5, including 23-2 in conference play (previously in the Big West Conference, Western Athletic Conference and the Mountain West Conference).
Utah State (1-4) beat Troy 21-10 last Saturday to snap a five-game skid, which began with a 25-24 home loss to Boise State in the 2025 regular-season finale.

Boise State went 89 yards in just six plays on its opening drive and took a 7-0 lead on Riley's 5-yard rushing TD. Jake Ripp returned an interception 21 yards for a touchdown that made it 28-7 late in the second quarter.

Javen Jacobs rushed for a 63-yard gain and two plays later caught a 1-yard touchdown pass from Grady Brosterhous in the second quarter. Kian Afrookhte made a 28-yard field goal as time expired to make it 28-10 at halftime.
Utah State: The Aggies' three previous losses this season came against teams that went into Saturday with a combined record of 11-1: Idaho State (4-0), Washington (3-1) and Utah (4-0).
Boise State: The Broncos have won 90 consecutive games when they score 35-plus points, dating to a 36-35 home loss to TCU on Nov. 12, 2011.

title: Rutherford, Stephen F. Austin beat Incarnate Word 28-26 for 16th straight regular-season win
summary: Gavin Rutherford threw three touchdown passes to help Stephen F
story: Gavin Rutherford threw three touchdown passes to help Stephen F

NACOGDOCHES, Texas -- Gavin Rutherford threw three touchdown passes Saturday night to help Stephen F. Austin beat Incarnate Word 28-26, the Lumberjacks' 16th consecutive win in the regular season and 11th straight in Southland Conference play.
The Lumberjacks (6-0, 3-0 Southland Conference), ranked No. 7 in the Stats Perform poll, are off to their best start since they started the 1995 season with a program-record seven straight wins.
Stephen F. Austin, which also extended its home win streak to 11 games, hasn’t lost a conference game since UIW beat the Lumberjacks 27-20 on Nov. 16, 2024 to claim the Southland title.
Emmett Brown was 27-of-52 passing for 373 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions for Incarnate Word (2-3, 1-1). Jeremiah Young had a career-high three sacks.

Brown threw a 53-yard touchdown pass to Jacob Emmers with 22 seconds left. After an offensive pass interference penalty took away his pass to Price Morgan for the 2-point conversion, Brown’s pass to Jayden Hibbler fell incomplete and the Lumberjacks held on.
David Rasor rushed for a 1-yard touchdown that capped a 10-play, 70-yard drive and gave Incarnate Word its first lead at 20-14 about 6 1/2 minutes into the third quarter.
Rutherford connected with Preston Alford for an 8-yard TD catch-and-run 4 1/2 minutes later and hit Clayton Wayland for an 8-yard touchdown on the first play of the fourth quarter that made it 28-20.
Lumberjacks kicker Carlos Alvarado missed field-goal attempts from 29, 56 (blocked by Young) and 43 yards, the last of which came with 48 seconds left.
Sophomore Makai Frisby, a Norfolk State transfer, had his fourth interception this season for the Lumberjacks.

title: Taylor runs for 2 TDs and Colts beat Commanders 30-13 in London
summary: Jonathan Taylor rushed for two touchdowns and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones ran one in and Indianapolis beat Washington 30-13 after the Commanders lost yet another quarterback to injury on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium
story: Jonathan Taylor rushed for two touchdowns and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones ran one in and Indianapolis beat Washington 30-13 after the Commanders lost yet another quarterback to injury on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium

LONDON -- Jonathan Taylor rushed for two touchdowns and Colts quarterback Daniel Jones ran one in and Indianapolis beat Washington 30-13 after the Commanders lost yet another quarterback to injury on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Marcus Mariota, who was starting in place of the injured Jayden Daniels, left the game after Washington’s second drive because of a knee injury. The veteran quarterback was sacked and didn’t return for the Commanders (1-3).

Third-string rookie quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis threw his first NFL touchdown pass to cut Indy's lead to 17-13 in the third quarter, but the Colts (2-2) answered with Spencer Shrader's 52-yard field goal and Jones' 4-yard run early in the fourth quarter.
Taylor rushed for 95 yards on 20 carries as the Colts overcame two turnovers from Jones, who completed 19 of 34 passes for 134 yards with an interception and a fumble.

Kaliakmanis threw a costly interception early in the third quarter and the Colts quickly capitalized. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies picked off Kaliakmanis' pass at the Washington 27 and returned it to the 20. Taylor’s second 5-yard run of the game made it 17-6.

Kaliakmanis bounced back on the next drive, though, hitting Treylon Burks on a 47-yard touchdown pass that closed the gap to 17-13. Burks got past cornerback Sauce Gardner and found space before hauling in the deep ball.
Shrader later added a 44-yard field goal — his third of the game — to extend Indy's lead to 30-13.
Kaliakmanis completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards with one touchdown and the interception.
The Colts led 10-6 at halftime after Taylor's first 5-yard touchdown run — which he celebrating by pantomiming drinking tea — and then Shrader’s 48-yard field goal.
The Commanders failed to capitalize on two red zone opportunities in the first quarter, settling for field goals.

Odafe Oweh drove Colts left tackle Bernhard Raimann backward into Jones causing the quarterback to fumble on Indy's first drive. Oweh then recovered it at the 21. The Commanders had fourth-and-2 from the 13 but opted for Drew Stevens' 31-yarder.

Washington then stalled at the Colts 5 on their next drive. On third down, Mariota was sacked at the 11 by Adetomiwa Adebawore and Laiatu Latu. Mariota walked off gingerly to the sideline, and another Stevens field goal made it 6-0, but the quarterback didn't return.

Attendance was 60,907 for the 13th NFL game played at Tottenham. The league had recently reduced remaining ticket prices to 79 pounds ($105) including for some high-end seats. Attendance has never been below 60,000 in previous games. The venue opened in 2019 and features an NFL field below the Premier League team’s moveable soccer pitch. It was 70 degrees Fahrenheit at kickoff.
Colts: LT Bernhard Raimann was hurt early in the third quarter.
Commanders: In addition to Mariota, WR Jaylin Lane was evaluated for a concussion ... DE Charles Omenihu had a groin problem... S Tyler Owens left with a hamstring injury.
Colts: at Pittsburgh next Sunday.
Commanders: host New York Giants next Sunday.
