Fox News Digital repeatedly reached out to Ambassador Zomlot for comment but did not receive a response.
Amelie Botbol is a freelance field reporter based in Tel Aviv, Israel, who reports on Israel-related news.

title: Taiwan analysts say Trump-Xi summit produced no policy shift but real test lies ahead
summary: Taiwan analysts assess whether Xi Jinping secured private concessions from Trump, with arms sales and senior U.S. official visits as key tests ahead.
story: The Chinese president departed the United States after a two-and-a-half-day summit that covered everything from AI to the future of Taiwan.

TAIPEI — Taiwanese officials were watching carefully for signs of policy changes toward the island as President Donald Trump hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping for a state visit last week in Washington, D.C.

Xi’s visit was of high interest in Taiwan, a regular target of China’s threats. On Saturday, a panel that included scholars, a retired U.S. military officer and Taiwan’s deputy foreign minister at the Institute for National Policy Research (INPR) in Taipei assessed what the third Trump–Xi meeting of Trump’s current term means for Taiwan. Most expect no change in U.S. policy toward Taiwan.

"Both of them got what they want and what they need," Kuo Yu-jen, INPR’s vice president and a professor at National Sun Yat-sen University’s Institute of China and Asia-Pacific Studies, told Fox News Digital. Trump can point to economic results from negotiating with Xi, while Xi can return to Beijing with the prestige of a high-profile U.S. reception, Kuo said. He called claims by some that Trump had "sold out" Taiwan excessive speculation.
XI PRAISES US STATE VISIT 'PERFECTION' AS TRUMP CALLS MEETINGS 'VERY PRODUCTIVE'
China's President Xi Jinping arrives to welcome President Donald Trump at the Great Hall of the People, Thursday, May 14, 2026, in Beijing. (Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo)

As expected, Xi reportedly pressed Trump to say the United States opposes Taiwan independence. Washington’s preferred description is that it does not support Taiwan independence, a distinction that, much to the relief of Taiwan government officials, Trump maintained.

Speaking exclusively to Fox News Digital after the forum, Taiwan’s Deputy Foreign Minister François Wu said Beijing wants more than a change in diplomatic language. It wants the world to view Taiwan as a domestic Chinese issue. If that argument succeeds, Wu said, Beijing could claim other countries have no right to respond to its actions against the island.
Taiwan’s Deputy Foreign Minister François Wu speaks at the Institute for National Policy Research (INPR) in Taipei on Sept. 26, 2026. (Eryk Michael Smith for Fox News Digital)

"The so-called independence of Taiwan is just an issue made specifically by the Chinese government," Wu said. Taiwan already has a president and government elected by its people, territory and its own currency, he said. "We just don’t need to declare any independence. We are a sovereign country."

Wu had expressed concerns prior to Trump’s visit to China in May, when he told Bloomberg that "What we are most afraid of is to put Taiwan on the menu of the talk between Xi Jinping and President Trump."

China’s Foreign Ministry claims Xi urged Trump to maintain the "correct position" to oppose Taiwan independence. Taiwan’s Foreign Ministry rushed out an objection on a public holiday in Taiwan, and repeated Taiwan’s own clear position on its sovereignty.
CHINA DEPLOYED OVER 100 VESSELS NEAR TAIWAN IN THE WAKE OF TRUMP-XI SUMMIT, TAIWAN SECURITY OFFICIAL CLAIMS

Soldiers pose for group photos with a Taiwan flag after a preparedness enhancement drill simulating the defense against Beijing's military intrusions, ahead of the Lunar New Year in Kaohsiung City, Taiwan, on Jan. 11, 2023. (Daniel Ceng/AP Photo)

The White House summary of Xi’s visit announced no change in Taiwan policy and instead emphasized more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion in goods in each direction, an AI incident communication channel and U.S. concerns about rare earth and critical-mineral supplies.

The visit nonetheless raised questions in Taiwan about what Xi might have obtained from Trump in private. Analysts cautioned that if there was a deal over Taiwan, it would only become clear in the coming months. Taiwan awaits Trump’s approval for more arms sales, visits to Taiwan by senior U.S. officials and a potential transit stop in the U.S. for Taiwan’s president. China objects to all of these, so how Trump handles them must balance relations with China, maintaining support for Taiwan and Trump’s priorities.

Dong Li-wen, executive director of the government-funded Foundation on Asia-Pacific Peace Studies, described the leaders’ shared approach as delaying difficult decisions while waiting for circumstances to change. For Xi, Dong argued, that is a longer-term strategy. For Trump, it is a temporary tactic. The two sides can keep talking and set aside issues they cannot settle, but their underlying competition remains.

The argument over Taiwan’s status is almost 80 years old. China claims the island as its territory, but the People’s Republic of China has not governed it for even a single day. The Republic of China government relocated to Taiwan after the Chinese Nationalists lost the civil war to Mao Zedong’s Communists in 1949.

President Donald Trump suggested Monday that U.S. arms sales to Taiwan could factor into broader negotiations with China, drawing a swift response from Taiwan’s president and reigniting debate in Washington over the future of longstanding U.S. policy toward the island. (Ann Wang/File Photo/Reuters)

The governing Democratic Progressive Party’s 1999 Resolution on Taiwan’s Future described Taiwan as an independent sovereign state called the Republic of China under its existing constitution. All of Taiwan’s democratically elected presidents have said something similar in interviews with international media, including Lee Teng-hui to The Washington Post in 1997, Chen Shui-bian to the BBC in 2010, Ma Ying-jeou to CNN in 2010, and Tsai Ing-wen to the BBC in 2020. Current President William Lai Ching-te said the same thing to Time in 2024, adding an oft-repeated insistence that the Republic of China and the People’s Republic of China are not subordinate to each other.

That status quo — which amounts to Taiwan being a de facto independent state — is what Taiwan intends to defend, according to Deputy Foreign Minister Wu. Xi left Washington having restated China’s demands. Analysts at the gathering said whether Xi managed to nudge U.S. policy in any way will soon be tested in decisions over arms sales and other issues, with some predicting weapons packages could be scaled down or "unbundled."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Speaking separately to Fox News Digital, Ross Darrell Feingold, a political analyst and assistant professor at Tamkang University’s Department of Diplomacy and International Relations, noted that with a local election in Taiwan this November, followed by presidential and legislative elections in January 2028, Taiwan’s domestic politics could also be a factor in U.S. decisions. "Although the U.S. is likely to back President Lai’s re-election; agreeing to arms sales, visits by Trump administration officials or Lai’s desired transit stop in the U.S. will need to be balanced against coming across as too blatantly interfering in Taiwan’s election, as well as the inevitable anger from China."

Eryk Michael Smith is a Taiwan-based correspondent who since 2007, has worked both as a broadcast journalist for the island's only English-language radio station, ICRT, as well as with numerous other publications and local news outlets. Smith's journalism focuses on Taiwan-China relations, local politics, as well as science and technology developments in the greater China region. He is based in Taiwan's largest southern city, Kaohsiung. He can be followed @ErykSmithTaiwan

title: US military completes withdrawal of troops from Iraq after 12-year mission
summary: The U.S. military completed its withdrawal from Erbil Air Base, ending Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq while relocating its headquarters to Jordan.
story: President Donald Trump announced U.S. troops will leave Iraq by the end of September, ending a 23-year presence.
The U.S. military has completed the withdrawal of American forces and equipment from Erbil Air Base in Iraq, ending its Operation Inherent Resolve mission, U.S. Central Command announced Wednesday.

The departure closes the Iraq chapter of the U.S.-led military mission launched against ISIS in 2014, while shifting primary responsibility for the country's security to Iraqi forces. The broader counter-ISIS campaign is not ending, however, with the U.S.-led task force relocating its headquarters to Jordan and operations continuing in Syria.
"Job well done to the tens of thousands of American service members, diplomats, and civilian personnel who answered the call in Iraq," CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper said.
US SERVICE MEMBER KILLED IN IRAQ AS TROOPS RECOVER UNIDENTIFIED REMAINS IN JORDAN: CENTCOM
Soldiers from the U.S.-led coalition forces are seen during the handover of the K1 Air Base to the Iraqi Army from the U.S.-led coalition in Kirkuk, Iraq on March 29, 2020. (The Associated Press)

"Because of your grit, sacrifice and professionalism, ISIS no longer poses a systemic threat to Iraq’s national security and Iraqi security forces, including the Peshmerga and other Iraqi Kurdistan Region security forces, now possess the capacity, leadership, and operational independence to unilaterally manage threats to their homeland," Cooper said.

Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell called the departure the formal conclusion of Operation Inherent Resolve in Iraq and said it marked a transition "from a wartime coalition mission to an Iraqi-led security effort supported by a more normal bilateral security relationship."
MOTORCYCLE PATROLS IRANIAN CITIES, CHECKPOINTS RISE AS REGIME BRACES FOR UNREST

The Pentagon said the U.S. will continue providing targeted training and intelligence support to Iraqi forces even after the withdrawal, while Iraqi security forces, including the Peshmerga, take the lead in keeping ISIS remnants suppressed.

Erbil Air Base in northern Iraq served as the main operational hub for Combined Joint Task Force — Operation Inherent Resolve and hosted most of the roughly 1,500 American and coalition forces supporting counter-ISIS operations, according to CENTCOM.

U.S. and coalition forces began leaving federal Iraq last October as Washington and Baghdad moved toward a bilateral defense relationship. The final removal of personnel and equipment from Erbil completed that transition on Sept. 30. The withdrawal followed an agreement reached between Washington and Baghdad under the Biden administration in 2024 and carried forward under the Trump administration.

Admiral Charles Bradford "Brad" Cooper II, commander of U.S. Central Command, speaks during a joint press conference at CENTCOM headquarters at MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa, Florida, on March 5, 2026. (Octavio Jones/AFP via Getty Images)

Combined Joint Task Force — Operation Inherent Resolve remains active and is now headquartered in Jordan, according to CENTCOM. U.S. forces also continue counter-ISIS operations in Syria alongside coalition partners and the Syrian government.
SYRIA OFF US TERROR BLACKLIST AFTER NEARLY 50 YEARS AS TRUMP ADMIN CLEARS INVESTMENT HURDLE

The U.S. has roughly 4,000 troops stationed in Jordan, where American forces will continue monitoring the ISIS threat. Muwaffaq Salti Air Base hosts U.S. combat aircraft and has itself become a target during the conflict with Iran. Three U.S. service members were killed in an Iranian attack on the base in July.

"As we step back and hand full primary responsibility for Iraq’s security to the Government of Iraq and the brave people of Iraq, U.S. and coalition forces stationed across the region will remain ready to respond to any ISIS threats that arise," Cooper said.
"Maintaining our vigilance and readiness is essential to protecting the U.S. homeland and strengthening regional security," he added.

The withdrawal ends a U.S. military presence in Iraq that was reestablished in 2014, when Iraqi authorities sought international assistance as ISIS captured large areas of the country. U.S. troops had previously left Iraq in 2011 following the 2003 invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein.

With U.S. forces leaving by Sept. 30 and as Baghdad tries to rein in Iran-backed militias, Iraq could also be entering its most dangerous period since ISIS seized Mosul in 2014. (REUTERS/Mohammed Ameen)

For the last several years, roughly 2,500 U.S. troops have been stationed in Iraq. The majority departed last year, leaving hundreds of troops in the northern Kurdish region until the final withdrawal.

The final departure comes as Iraq faces a separate security challenge from powerful Iran-backed militias operating inside the country. Baghdad has sought to bring weapons held by non-state groups under government control, but some of the most influential militias have resisted disarming.
IRANIAN PRESIDENT BLAMES US FOR MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT WHILE DENYING NUCLEAR AMBITIONS, OFFERS TO DILUTE URANIUM
The Pentagon explicitly identified those militias as one of the security challenges Baghdad will now be expected to confront.

"The primary responsibility for addressing Iraq's remaining security challenges, including ISIS remnants and Iran-aligned militias that undermine Iraqi sovereignty and regional stability, now rests with the Government of Iraq," Parnell said.

The withdrawal also reduces the number of U.S. military targets inside Iraq after American forces there faced repeated attacks by Iran-aligned groups following Hamas' Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel. During this year's war with Iran, seven of the 18 U.S. service members killed in Iranian attacks were killed in Iraq, according to Fox News reporting.

The withdrawal has drawn sharply different reactions inside Iraq. Iran-aligned groups celebrated the U.S. departure, while officials in the country's Kurdish region have raised concerns about the loss of American air-defense capabilities amid drone and missile threats.

Kurdish officials say their region has faced more than 1,000 Iranian drone and ballistic missile attacks since the war with Iran began Feb. 28, adding to concerns over the removal of U.S. forces and air-defense capabilities.

Thousands of ISIS fighters also remain in Iraq and Syria despite the collapse of the terror group's organized military threat. The Iraqi government has said its forces will continue operations against ISIS, while the Pentagon said the U.S. remains committed to preventing the group from reconstituting from Iraqi territory.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
CENTCOM said U.S. and coalition forces elsewhere in the region will remain prepared to respond if ISIS again poses a threat.

"The United States supports a strong sovereign Iraq that secures its borders, protects its people, and serves as the foundation for deeper commercial, diplomatic, and security cooperation between our two countries," Parnell said.
Fox News' Liz Friden and the Associated Press contributed to this report.
Bradford Betz is a Fox News Digital breaking reporter covering crime, political issues, and much more.

title: FlyDubai passenger says co-pilot stabbed captain before terrifying plunge, emergency landing
summary: A passenger says a FlyDubai co-pilot stabbed the captain before the Israel-bound flight plunged, triggering hijacking fears and an emergency diversion.
story: Fox News foreign correspondent Jeff Paul reports on an Israel-bound flight emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The Jerusalem Post's Amichai Stein and Vice Admiral Robert Harward analyze the cockpit attack on 'The Faulkner Focus.'

A FlyDubai passenger said the co-pilot apparently stabbed the captain during a cockpit altercation before the Israel-bound jet plunged thousands of feet, triggering a terrifying scene aboard the aircraft and an emergency diversion to Saudi Arabia Wednesday.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later said one of the pilots stabbed the other and apparently attempted to crash the aircraft, which was carrying mostly Israeli passengers. Netanyahu said a passenger and crew member managed to enter the cockpit and overpower the alleged attacker as he tried to sabotage the aircraft's systems, allowing another crew member to stabilize the plane.

"I salute the heroes who showed extraordinary bravery and, according to the passenger's account, saved many lives," Netanyahu said, according to an unofficial translation of his remarks. He added that the pilot accused of carrying out the stabbing was arrested and was being investigated by Saudi authorities.
The passenger told Fox News that accounts of what happened remained conflicting, but said passengers understood that the co-pilot had stabbed the captain and then collapsed onto the controls.
A FlyDubai passenger with blood seen on his shirt (X/@AmichaiStein1)

"There are many different accounts, but apparently the co-pilot stabbed the captain and collapsed onto the controls, shutting down the entire instrument panel. We began plunging downward for several minutes. Everyone on the plane was screaming, the overhead compartments opened, and the power went out. We were sure we were going to die. It was very scary," the passenger said.

FlyDubai later confirmed that an "altercation occurred in the flight deck," saying on-duty FlyDubai crew traveling aboard the flight secured the aircraft, diverted it and landed safely in Tabuk. The airline did not confirm the reported stabbing and said the underlying reasons and motives remained under formal investigation.
LIVE UPDATES: FLYDUBAI PILOT STABS FELLOW PILOT, ATTEMPTS TO CRASH PLANE, NETANYAHU SAYS

Israeli passenger Haim Lazarovich, who experienced an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, during a flight on FlyDubai plane, arrives at Ben Gurion International Airport, near Tel Aviv, Israel, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026. (Ariel Schalit/AP)
Saudi Arabia's Tabuk airport said both pilots were hospitalized after suffering injuries, according to Reuters. An investigation into the incident remains underway.
The Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, and everyone aboard was reported safe, according to officials.

A regional official briefed on the incident said an altercation broke out in the cockpit and apparently involved the pilots, though it was not immediately clear what sparked the confrontation. Israeli media, citing security officials, also reported that a dispute between the two pilots was behind the emergency.
"The crew have been questioned as part of the investigation," the regional official said, according to The Associated Press.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu embraces passenger Yaniv Hayun on Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026. Netanyahu's office said Hayun "broke into the cockpit" on the FlyDubai plane, helping save the aircraft. (Kobi Gideon/GPO)
A U.S. official later told Fox News that the alleged attacker was taken into custody when the plane landed in Saudi Arabia.

The incident prompted an immediate security response in Israel, where authorities initially feared the plane — carrying more than 100 Israeli passengers, according to The Jerusalem Post — could have been hijacked. Israel scrambled fighter jets as the situation unfolded.
AMERICANS WARNED AGAINST TRAVEL PLANS AS TERRORISM THREATENS POPULAR DESTINATION

Passengers who experienced an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia, during a flight on FlyDubai plane, arrive at Ben Gurion International Airport, near Tel Aviv, Israel, on Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026.  (Ariel Schalit/AP)

Two Israeli officials told Reuters that Israel's assessment was that the incident may have been an attempted "terror attack." The Jerusalem Post separately reported that the growing assessment among Israel's security establishment, including the IDF, Mossad and Shin Bet, was that the incident was intended as an act of terror.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz went further, calling the incident an "attempted jihadist terrorist attack" that was thwarted by Israeli passengers who entered the cockpit and overpowered the alleged attacker.
"According to the preliminary information available to us, the terrorist had one intention: to crash the aircraft with everyone on board," Katz said.

The aircraft transmitted an emergency alert during the flight, according to publicly available flight-tracking information. Flight FZ1073 had departed Dubai and was headed for Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv before diverting to Tabuk.
Flightradar24 data showed the aircraft suddenly plunging nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the first emergency signal, according to Reuters.

A FlyDubai aircraft carrying Israelis who experienced an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia is seen parked at Ben Gurion International Airport, near Tel Aviv, Israel, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026.  (Ariel Schalit/AP)

"The flight from Dubai was a very calm one for the first two hours. And when we were at the Jordanian border, suddenly the aircraft dropped, like a massive drop, like a massive turbulence for 20-30 seconds. Then balanced, and then once again dropped for 10 seconds and balanced again," passenger Almog Italie said in a video obtained by Reuters. "And then we saw that in the front of the aircraft there was a riot. Many people rushed over there. Apparently, one pilot stabbed the other."

Capt. Meidan Barr, former chairman of the Israel Airline Pilot Association, told Fox News Channel that such a rapid loss of altitude would ordinarily resemble an emergency descent, such as one performed following a loss of cabin pressure.

"Losing like 15,000 feet in two or three minutes, that is something that you do in, like, an emergency descent when you lose pressure," Barr said, adding that the aircraft's safe landing was significant and would allow investigators to determine what went wrong.
A plane takes off as a FlyDubai aircraft sits on the tarmac at Dubai International Airport in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026. (AP Photo)

Flight-tracking data also showed the aircraft transmitting emergency transponder code 7700 before briefly switching to 7500, a code used to signal unlawful interference with an aircraft, and later returning to 7700.

Passengers described a tense scene aboard the aircraft as the emergency unfolded. Travelers told Israel's Channel 12 by phone that they heard shouting from passengers near the front of the plane who had apparently heard the cockpit altercation. They also said the aircraft dipped steeply before landing in Saudi Arabia.
IRISH SOCCER PLAYERS WEAR BLACK ARMBANDS, REFUSE TO SHAKE HANDS AHEAD OF CONTENTIOUS MATCH VS ISRAEL

The account provided directly to Fox News offered a more harrowing description of the sudden descent, with the passenger saying people screamed as overhead compartments opened and power aboard the aircraft went out.
Yasmin Abukasis, whose daughter was aboard the flight, told Fox News at Ben Gurion International Airport that her daughter described passengers rushing to intervene during the cockpit confrontation.

Abukasis said her daughter told her that a man had a knife and that passengers grabbed his hand and forced him to the floor amid significant bleeding. She also said two other pilots subsequently took control of the aircraft.
After landing, passengers remained aboard the plane as a heavy Saudi security presence surrounded the aircraft, according to their accounts to the Israeli outlet.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office later said the situation was under control. The scare came as Netanyahu has warned in recent days about unspecified heightened security threats facing Israel.

Netanyahu convened security consultations over the incident and cleared the remainder of his schedule to manage the crisis, according to Reuters. The Jerusalem Post reported that Israeli airspace was temporarily closed before reopening after the aircraft landed in Saudi Arabia.

FlyDubai said it deployed two replacement aircraft to Tabuk to relieve the passengers and crew and that the incident had no impact on its other scheduled operations. A FlyDubai plane carrying the passengers later landed safely in Tel Aviv on Wednesday evening local time.

"The plane was falling down... and then I felt that I am losing it, and I am going to lose all of my family. My wife was beside me, my little boy was also beside me and I was separated from them... it was very, very terrifying," passenger Haim Lazarovich said at the terminal at Ben Gurion Airport after landing.
"There was a group of young people and they fought with the second pilot," Lazarovich added, noting that he sat at the front of the plane. "Thank God I’m alive."

A FlyDubai spokesperson said "at this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation," and, "we urge all parties to refrain from premature speculation while authorities gather the facts."
The exact circumstances surrounding the reported cockpit confrontation remained unclear Wednesday.

While disputes between pilots serious enough to affect a flight are rare, similar incidents have occurred. Two Air France pilots were suspended in 2022 after fighting in the cockpit during a flight from Geneva to Paris. That aircraft did not divert and landed as scheduled.

The initial hijacking fears carried particular weight in Israel, where aviation security has long been shaped by a history of attacks on Israeli travelers and aircraft. Palestinian militants carried out a series of hijackings and attacks involving Israelis during the 1960s and 1970s. Israel has not experienced an aircraft hijacking in decades and maintains stringent security procedures for Israel-bound flights.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

FlyDubai is a lower-cost sister carrier of Emirates. Flights between Israel and the United Arab Emirates began after the two countries normalized relations in 2020, opening the UAE as a major destination for Israeli travelers.
Fox News' Yonat Friling, Greg Norman-Diamond, David Spunt, Jake Gibson, Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Bradford Betz is a Fox News Digital breaking reporter covering crime, political issues, and much more.

title: U.S. Air Force removes all bombers from British air base targeted in a suspected terrorist plot
summary: The bombers at RAF Fairford “have been re-deployed to their home stations in the United States,” a Pentagon official told NBC News.
story: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Air Force has brought home all of its bombers stationed at RAF Fairford, a U.S.-run military air base in England used to strike Iran, following an investigation into a planned terrorist attack at the base.
A Defense Department official told NBC News that all bombers that had been deployed to the base “have been re-deployed to their home stations in the United States.”

“The Airmen that operate America’s bomber force, including B-1s, B-2s, and B-52s, remain ready to deliver precision global strike capabilities — including through operations that launch and recover from the continental United States — anywhere, anytime,” the official said.
The rushed withdrawal of at least 12 bombers included several that had just arrived as part of a rotation to the base, two Pentagon officials told NBC News.

Aviation watchers, such as the Military Air Tracking Alliance, have observed dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of RAF Fairford since the opening days of the Iran war. Observers noticed a host of B-1 bombers flying out of the base Sunday.
President Donald Trump is weighing options for his war on Iran — including new strikes — despite his initial promises to Americans that the campaign would last a matter of weeks.

“We have decisions that I’ll make about Iran. Iran’s been decimated. So the only question is — it’ll either be the easy way, or the hard way,” Trump told reporters Saturday as he left the White House for a rally in Ohio.
For Subscribers

A dual British-Iranian national was arrested in central London last week on suspicion of plotting a terrorist attack following a security incident at RAF Fairford in late September. In total, six people have been taken into custody and released on bail during the investigation.
For Subscribers
British authorities have linked the incident to Tehran. Iran has denied involvement.
American bombers have used the air base, 100 miles west of London, during decades of conflicts in the Middle East.

The U.S. military still maintains a sizable presence in the Middle East. On Thursday, a U.S. official said the recently deployed USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and the USS Malkin Island amphibious readiness group — a group of ships that together carry over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines — are heading for the region. The official said the move could have three carriers in the region as early as the end of October.

title: How the shooting death of a Houston father is igniting Latino politics in Texas
summary: Lorenzo Salgado Araujo was killed on his way to work by ICE agents, who said he used his vehicle as a weapon. The community is demanding justice.
story: HOUSTON — As the sun set on a late September evening, a voice rose over the din of traffic at the roadside memorial for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, the 52-year-old husband and father fatally shot here by immigration authorities three months ago.
Sitting on barbershop steps, Berta Lopez, a nearby resident, alternately sang, recited prayers and cried for a man she never met.

“It was unjust — he was killed unjustly! The family is deeply hurt, his wife, his children. They are like family to us. And why don’t they show the people who did the killing? Why don’t they show them? Why don’t they release the names of the people who killed Lorenzo? Why don’t they expose them?” she said in Spanish.

In tears, Lopez said that after more than a year of intensive operations by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Salgado Araujo’s killing was a clarifying moment. The government, she said, saw those who weren’t U.S. citizens as less than nothing. She was tired of it.

“Just because we’re Hispanic, shouldn’t we hold our heads high? No, God doesn’t want us hanging our heads in shame. He wants all of us, his children, to hold our heads up high,” Lopez said. “God doesn’t care about papers.”

Lopez’s hurt and anger were reflected in NBC News interviews with more than three dozen Houston-area Latinos, elected officials, activists and political strategists. They reveal a distraught community whose members feel degraded by the messages they hear out of Washington, D.C., during President Donald Trump’s second term. They said they have been terrorized by the constant stories of those detained, many wrongly, and left to languish. They were aghast that the government was sending immigrants to countries they had never heard of.

Many said Salgado Araujo’s shooting death crystallized their feelings of powerlessness. Most Latinos were better versed in the details of the incident than in the names and backgrounds of those running for some of the highest-profile offices in their state.
Their refrains were in the same vein: That could have been my dad, my brother, my uncle, my son — or me.

title: Poll: Latino voters swing away from Trump and Republicans
summary: Democrats have a significant lead among Latino voters in 2026 amid economic concerns, according to the NBC News/Telemundo poll.
story: Latino voters helped propel Donald Trump back to the White House. Now, they are turning on him, according to a new NBC News/Telemundo poll — a shift that gives Democrats a major opportunity to capitalize in a 2026 election that could hinge on states and districts with sizable Latino populations.

Like the broader electorate, Latino voters are racked by major concerns about high prices and Trump’s approach to immigration enforcement. The president’s approval rating sits at 27% among Latino voters. Two-thirds say his administration’s deportation policies have gone too far and three-quarters disapprove of how he has handled the economy and the cost of living.

title: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
summary: The woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by Cornell University fraternity members has received threats pressuring her to drop her lawsuit, her attorney said.
story: The woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by Cornell University fraternity members has received threats pressuring her to drop her lawsuit, her attorney said.

Thomas Giuffra told CNN’s “State of the Union” that people attempting to unmask his client’s identity had also targeted at least three women mistakenly identified as her. The former Cornell student is identified as Jane Doe in court documents.

Doe filed a lawsuit last month against Cornell and seven Chi Phi fraternity members, alleging she was sexually assaulted over the course of hours on Oct. 19 and 20, 2024, while she was under the influence of ketamine, alcohol and marijuana.

The suit has sparked renewed scrutiny of how the university and local authorities handled the allegations. Gov. Kathy Hochul last week appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to consider whether criminal charges are appropriate.

2024 investigation: Cornell police spoke to witnesses and received anonymous tips about an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house in the first weeks of its investigation two years ago. But the local prosecutor did not review the additional information before deciding not to bring charges.Arrest at Chi Phi: Police records also show that university police made a drug-related arrest at a fraternity house 22 hours before the woman alleged she was drugged and sexually assaulted there.President’s statement: Michael Kotlikoff said in a video message Saturday that what Doe alleges is “deeply disturbing” and raises questions about the investigation that followed.

2024 investigation: Cornell police spoke to witnesses and received anonymous tips about an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house in the first weeks of its investigation two years ago. But the local prosecutor did not review the additional information before deciding not to bring charges.
Arrest at Chi Phi: Police records also show that university police made a drug-related arrest at a fraternity house 22 hours before the woman alleged she was drugged and sexually assaulted there.
President’s statement: Michael Kotlikoff said in a video message Saturday that what Doe alleges is “deeply disturbing” and raises questions about the investigation that followed.

title: Cornell rape accuser faces threats demanding she drop her lawsuit, attorney says
summary: The accuser’s attorney said that women mistakenly identified as Jane Doe have also received threats and that he received one Sunday morning.
story: The woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by Cornell University fraternity members has received threats pressuring her to drop her lawsuit, her attorney said Sunday.

Thomas Giuffra told CNN’s “State of the Union” that people attempting to unmask his client’s identity had also targeted at least three women mistakenly identified as her. The former Cornell student is identified as Jane Doe in court documents.
“She’s received multiple threats, and women who aren’t even Jane Doe receive threats,” Giuffra said. He added that he had received a threat Sunday morning.
For Subscribers
Giuffra did not identify those responsible or say whether the threats had been reported to law enforcement. He did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for more information about the threats.

Jane Doe filed a lawsuit last month against Cornell and seven Chi Phi fraternity members, alleging she was sexually assaulted over the course of hours on Oct. 19-20, 2024, while she was under the influence of ketamine, alcohol and marijuana.
For Subscribers

The allegations have sparked renewed scrutiny of the university’s and local authorities’ handling of the allegations. Gov. Kathy Hochul last week appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to consider whether criminal charges are appropriate.

NBC News reported Friday that Cornell police interviewed witnesses and received anonymous tips during their investigation in 2024, but Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten did not review that additional information before deciding not to pursue charges at the time. He has defended his decision, saying that Jane Doe’s initial six-page statement to police did not allege criminality.
Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said Saturday that the university must do better and that its board of trustees would announce an independent review of its handling of the case next week.

title: ‘It’s not enough to not rape somebody’: How parents are talking to kids about Cornell
summary: Parents are using Jane Doe’s case to talk to their sons about resisting peer pressure and stepping in when something’s wrong, even if it means challenging their friends.
story: For parents following the case of a former Cornell student who alleges she was gang-raped at the Chi Phi house in October 2024, one question has been top of mind: Why did no one in the fraternity intervene?

In a lawsuit filed last month, a woman identified as Jane Doe said  she was sexually assaulted by Chi Phi members while she was under the influence of several substances. A screenshot of a group Snapchat between members, which was included in the lawsuit, showed one fraternity member saying there was “free p----” available upstairs where Jane Doe was.
Cornell agrees to outside investigation in assault case
The fraternity chapter was subsequently barred from campus, but no one was criminally charged. Prosecutors have reopened a criminal investigation into the allegations.

As the case continues to draw national attention, parents online are sharing how they’re teaching their children to challenge the culture that allows sexual violence to persist. Some have offered advice, suggesting parents pose questions to their kids like, “What have you heard about this story?” and “What questions do you have?” Others have posted candid conversations they’ve had with their kids about the case to help inspire others to do the same.
“I’m parenting to help them become the kind of man who stops this from happening,” Brian Recker, a former pastor with over 450,000 followers on Instagram, said in a video earlier this week.

“It’s not enough to not rape somebody. Because what that girl could’ve really used that night and what she didn’t find was one good man,” Recker added. “One good man in that group chat who would have been willing to risk some social shame from his frat bros, who was willing to put her safety above the approval of men who would hurt her.”

Recker told NBC News that he approaches the subject differently with his 9-year-old twins and his 11-year-old son. With his younger sons, he focuses on their own safety. But as his oldest enters middle school, Recker has asked him to consider what he would do if messages like those described in the Cornell case appeared in one of his group chats.
He views these types of conversations with his sons as a way to “plant seeds” that shape their approach to the world as they grow up.

“It is so easy to just be silent and not want to rock the boat, especially if you think that that’s going to cause other boys, other men to look down on you,” he said. “But I do believe, especially in the early years, we have the opportunity to shape reality for them in some really important ways, and to let them know what kind of world they’re entering, and to prepare them.”

But sexual assault can be an especially difficult topic to tackle with kids, particularly for parents who have their own trauma history, said Sumi Raghavan, a psychologist who was also among those sharing how they spoke to their kids about the Cornell case.
Raghavan said she urges fellow parents to feel empowered to discuss tough topics, noting that some level of discomfort is normal when it comes to these conversations.

Research links open parent-child communication with healthier relationships and safer decision-making. Raghavan said that means that even as kids and teens begin to care more about their peers’ opinions than their parents’, they’re still likely to view their parents as anchors for major decisions.

“One of the most powerful messages you’re sending when you’re willing to have these conversations is that you are a person who they can talk to, and you are demonstrating that you are unafraid of these topics,” she said.

Psychologist Becky Kennedy, the founder of parenting advice service Good Inside, had similar guidance — though she cautioned that parents should also be careful to not treat conversations with their kids as “checking off a box.”

Kids build emotional skills from the patterns they experience growing up. For example, learning to want something and be OK with not getting it, Kennedy said. Often, parents want to say “no” to a child’s request but convince themselves to say “yes” due to fear of the child’s reaction.
“These are things that will play out for the rest of a boy’s life, and eventually, maybe in sexual situations,” she said. “But those patterns are established over and over in everyday interactions.”

Parents should also listen and try to understand when their child wants to say “no,” Kennedy said, rather than forging forward with a decision without considering why the child might be unwilling or uncomfortable. By doing the latter, she said, parents are unwittingly reinforcing the culture that makes it harder for kids to resist group pressure later in life.
Parents are bound to make mistakes, Kennedy said. But that shouldn’t keep them from trying to do things differently once they realize they want to change a pattern.

“It’s actually the whole thought that ‘it’s too late’ that stops us from acting differently in all of those situations,” Kennedy said. “The best way to not repeat a pattern is to actually bring new information to your kid and say, ‘You know what? In my parenting, I feel like I’ve been doing something that I’m not proud of. I learned something new. Here’s what I want to do differently the next time.’”

If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at https://www.rainn.org/get-help.

title: Early indications suggest Flydubai co-pilot acted alone in attack, officials say
summary: Officials cautioned that the investigation remains in its early stages and that possible links to an organization or foreign government haven’t been definitively ruled out.
story: TEL AVIV — Early indications suggest the Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain and trying to seize control of an Israel-bound plane acted alone, rather than as part of a larger organization or on behalf of a foreign government, multiple U.S. officials briefed on the investigation and a former Israeli security official told NBC News.
The U.S. officials cautioned that the investigation into Wednesday’s midair attack remains at an early stage.

“The assessment is that he operated alone. Right now, it looks like a case of ‘lone wolf’ terrorism inspired by content found online,” said Shalom Ben Hanan, a former official in the Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency.
“We still need to wait for the final investigation results to determine whether an organization or a state is behind it,” he added.

Emirati authorities, who are leading the investigation, said Saturday that the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash ax and attempted to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls in an attempted terrorist attack.

The flight was carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted when crew members and passengers entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials.

NBC News has identified the suspect as Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, based on information from multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East. Authorities have not released his identity.
UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said Saturday that investigators were working to establish the incident’s “full circumstances, motives, and any links.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The preliminary assessment comes after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that investigators were examining whether the attacker had been sent by someone.

President Donald Trump also raised the possibility of Iranian involvement Thursday, threatening renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack. A senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation previously told NBC News there were no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack.

The flight captain, Indian national Smit Machchhar, said Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi that he had been severely injured and could sense the aircraft descending before he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to intervene.
“I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Raf Sanchez and Paul Goldman reported from Tel Aviv and Tom Winter from New York.

title: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson exits game vs. Titans with ankle injury
summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson missed the second half of the Ravens’ 24-18 win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday because of an ankle injury.
story: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson missed the second half of the Ravens’ 24-18 win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday because of an ankle injury.

Jackson was on the sideline without a helmet during the Baltimore’s first possession of the third quarter, with the Ravens holding a 24-7 lead at the time. The team announced that he was questionable to return, but Jackson did not play another snap.
He was also seen wearing a boot on his left ankle after the game, according to ESPN.
Jackson was off to a hot start before leaving. He completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the first half. He also carried the ball twice for 20 yards.
He was tackled on the second to last play of the half and appeared to be favoring his ankle after going to the sideline. He was replaced by backup Tyler Huntley to start the third quarter.
Huntley finished the game completing 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards, and Baltimore did not score again.

In 2021, Jackson missed five games, and the Ravens went 1-4 without him, missing the playoffs. The following season, he again missed five games and didn’t play in Baltimore’s first-round playoff loss.

The Ravens entered Sunday with a 2-1 record, defeating the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys, with their only loss coming against the New Orleans Saints. Baltimore is now tied with the Cleveland Browns at the top of the AFC North after Sunday’s win.

Jackson, 29, is in his ninth season with Baltimore, which selected him with the final pick of the first round in the 2018 NFL draft. Entering Sunday, he had thrown for 745 yards and four touchdowns this season and run for one more score.
Jackson is in the second to last year of a five-year, $260 million contract he signed in March 2023. He and the Ravens reportedly did not seriously discuss a long-term extension before this season.

title: Who is the best team in the NFC East? Through four weeks, it’s anyone’s guess.
summary: Who will win the NFC East? After games for the Giants, Eagles and Cowboys all went down to the final seconds in Week 4, no one has separated itself yet.
story: Nearly one-quarter of the way through the NFL regular season, a hierarchy of contenders and pretenders is beginning to become defined in some divisions.
Just not in the NFC East.

A rash of down-to-the-wire results Sunday has left the division as up for grabs as any in the league, with no clear favorite to run away with the division title and the playoff spot that comes with it.
The New York Giants are 3-1 (1-0 in division play), but how long can their backup quarterbacks keep up a winning streak?

The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-2 and 1-0 in the division but have been outscored by 18 points overall, and neither star running back Saquon Barkley nor quarterback Jalen Hurts has done much to quiet offseason concern about their offense.

The Dallas Cowboys are 2-2, including 1-1 in the division, and remain one of the league’s biggest threats to score — just as their defense is still one of the least trustworthy to get stops. Only the Washington Commanders (1-3, 0-2) look like a nonfactor one month in after a lopsided 30-13 loss Sunday in London to Indianapolis.

Parity has historically been the norm in the NFC East, which had different teams win the division every year from 2003-04 to 2024-25. Not much separates them this fall, either. The Cowboys (plus-10) have the best scoring differential among the group, but the Giants (plus 3), the Eagles (minus 18) and the Commanders (minus 34) aren’t far behind.

The Los Angeles Rams saved their season with a last-minute comeback

The Giants’ playoff hopes appeared damaged two weeks ago after starting quarterback Jaxson Dart was lost for the season, leaving the team in the hands of the turnover-prone backup Jameis Winston.

And yet, the Giants have won two straight games to improve to 3-1. Sunday’s latest win, 36-24 against Arizona, was sealed only when defensive back Deonte Banks returned an interception 98 yards for a touchdown in the final seconds. It followed a nail-biting, 12-7 win last week against Tennessee that showed the limits of Winston, only for the 32-year-old former No. 1 overall pick to throw three touchdown passes against the Cardinals. The Giants also were the beneficiaries of three interceptions to win their first three home games of the season for the first time since 2008.

How sustainable is this? In addition to Dart’s season-ending injury, the Giants are without outside linebacker Brian Burns for the year, as well. It also was the first time since 2021-22 that Winston had won back-to-back games as a starter.
“We’re in a good position four games in, but it’s only four games in,” Giants coach John Harbaugh said. “We can play so much better.”
As that game was ending, so were two others that kept the division in flux.

In Philadelphia, the Eagles had an opportunity to boost their uneven early-season results with a win against the prohibitive preseason favorite to win the Super Bowl, the Los Angeles Rams. Leading 20-10 with 7:31 to play in the fourth quarter, the Eagles were 2 yards from the Rams’ end zone when coach Nick Sirianni opted against kicking a short field goal to try for what might have been a game-sealing touchdown.

When Hurts’ pass fell incomplete, though, the Rams answered with a 98-yard scoring drive, then added a second touchdown less than three minutes later to win, 24-20. If the game’s outcome shifted in the final minutes, there were warnings all afternoon for the Eagles, who were 0-for-12 on third down, the worst performance in franchise history.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“I know when we’re 0-for whatever we were today, everybody has a hand in that,” Sirianni said.
He called the fourth-down decision his own fault.
“We have to look at ourselves in the mirror,” Sirianni said. “We have to be accountable. I’ve got to do a better job. All of us have things to improve on.”

Barkley also continues to look little like the player who rushed for 2,000 yards in Philadelphia’s Super Bowl-winning season two years ago. He entered Sunday with 174 yards in three games. After two rushes for just 8 yards, Barkley left the game with an injury — ominously, making him the 10th Eagles starter to be hurt this season.

In the same 10-minute span in which Philadelphia saw a victory slip out of its grip while the Giants secured their own in the final minutes of the fourth quarter, Dallas had its own late drama to avoid a 1-3 start that would have been its worst through four games since 2020.

Trailing 30-26 with a little more than two minutes left, the Cowboys produced an 11-play drive that traveled 74 yards for the go-ahead score to beat Houston, 34-30. Dak Prescott’s game-winning touchdown pass went to CeeDee Lamb with 40 seconds left — because who else could it have been? Against a Houston defense that was one of the NFL’s best last season, Lamb was unstoppable, catching a career-high 17 passes for 189 yards. (Lamb came into Week 4 with 20 catches all season.)
Lamb joined Brandon Marshall (2009) and Terrell Owens (2000) as the only players since 2000 with at least 17 catches, 180 receiving yards and a touchdown.

The win could be seen as a response to earlier, dispiriting results. Last week, the Cowboys lost on a last-second field goal to Baltimore thanks to questionable decisions by coach Brian Schottenheimer, calls that he acknowledged to the team were his fault, according to a report. It wasn’t entirely on the offense, however. The Cowboys’ defense entered Sunday allowing opponents to convert 58.8% of third downs, the NFL’s worst mark. The Texans managed just 3-for-10.
“I just want Schotty to know that I got his back,” Lamb told reporters Sunday. “I’m with him. I’m one of his strongest soldiers. It’s just going to battle with each other.”

title: U.S. Air Force removes all bombers from British air base targeted in a suspected terrorist plot
summary: The bombers at RAF Fairford “have been re-deployed to their home stations in the United States,” a Pentagon official told NBC News.
story: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Air Force has brought home all of its bombers stationed at RAF Fairford, a U.S.-run military air base in England used to strike Iran, following an investigation into a planned terrorist attack at the base.
A Defense Department official told NBC News that all bombers that had been deployed to the base “have been re-deployed to their home stations in the United States.”

“The Airmen that operate America’s bomber force, including B-1s, B-2s, and B-52s, remain ready to deliver precision global strike capabilities — including through operations that launch and recover from the continental United States — anywhere, anytime,” the official said.
The rushed withdrawal of at least 12 bombers included several that had just arrived as part of a rotation to the base, two Pentagon officials told NBC News.

Aviation watchers, such as the Military Air Tracking Alliance, have observed dozens of B-52 and B-1 bombers operating out of RAF Fairford since the opening days of the Iran war. Observers noticed a host of B-1 bombers flying out of the base Sunday.
President Donald Trump is weighing options for his war on Iran — including new strikes — despite his initial promises to Americans that the campaign would last a matter of weeks.

“We have decisions that I’ll make about Iran. Iran’s been decimated. So the only question is — it’ll either be the easy way, or the hard way,” Trump told reporters Saturday as he left the White House for a rally in Ohio.
For Subscribers

A dual British-Iranian national was arrested in central London last week on suspicion of plotting a terrorist attack following a security incident at RAF Fairford in late September. In total, six people have been taken into custody and released on bail during the investigation.
For Subscribers
British authorities have linked the incident to Tehran. Iran has denied involvement.
American bombers have used the air base, 100 miles west of London, during decades of conflicts in the Middle East.

The U.S. military still maintains a sizable presence in the Middle East. On Thursday, a U.S. official said the recently deployed USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and the USS Malkin Island amphibious readiness group — a group of ships that together carry over 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines — are heading for the region. The official said the move could have three carriers in the region as early as the end of October.

Search for 6 aboard medical jet enters second day after crash near Nantucket

Governor says Tennessee’s prisons chief is resigning after failed execution of Christa Pike
The head of Tennessee’s prison system is resigning after the failed execution of Christa Pike, Gov. Bill Lee announced Saturday.
In response to the resignation news, Pike’s attorneys told NBC News that Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada’s departure was “justified, but it does nothing to help Christa now.”
“What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person,” they said. Pike remained unconscious in a hospital as of Friday.

Pike has remained unconscious and on a ventilator at a hospital in the four days since her failed execution in Tennessee, and her prognosis might not be known for days more, one of her lawyers said Sunday.

title: The Los Angeles Rams saved their season with a last-minute comeback
summary: The Los Angeles Rams, preseason Super Bowl favorites, may have saved their season with a come-from-behind win against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday.
story: After blowing a 16-0 lead to the Denver Broncos a week ago, the Los Angeles Rams — a preseason Super Bowl favorite — looked well on their way to another dispiriting loss Sunday.

The Rams were trailing 20-10 and had the ball 98 yards away from the end zone with less than eight minutes to go in the fourth quarter on a day they had already committed several mistakes against an opponent they had not beaten since 2020. Staring a 1-3 record in the face, Los Angeles instead stepped up and saved its season.

The Rams improved to 2-2 in Week 4, scoring two late touchdowns to beat the Philadelphia Eagles, 24-20. The win was Los Angeles coach Sean McVay’s first against Eagles coach Nick Sirianni, and absolved the Rams from a steep climb to make the playoffs.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Los Angeles came alive in the final half of the fourth quarter. After a fourth-down stop by the defense, reigning MVP Matthew Stafford led a 10-play, 98-yard drive — during which he completed seven passes — to first cut the lead to 20-17.

After a three-and-out by Philadelphia, the Rams once again went on a 10-play drive, this time covering 79 yards. The possession was capped by three Kyren Williams runs, the last of which Williams punched into the end zone after breaking a slew of tackles.
“By any freaking means, get your butt in the end zone,” Williams told the FOX broadcast postgame of his mindset during his game-winning score.
McVay said postgame Williams’ run was “gutsy.”
“If you say you wouldn’t want that guy in your foxhole, then you’re in the wrong foxhole,” he added.
Los Angeles’s late heroics made up for what was an otherwise sloppy effort.

Stafford was uneven. He completed 32 of 51 passes for 317 yards, but he threw for no touchdowns and two interceptions. Stafford has now thrown at least one pick in every game this season, and has six interceptions after throwing only eight all last season.

There were plenty of other miscues: A missed field goal, a pass interference penalty that led to a touchdown, a kickoff out of bounds, and a sideline interference penalty that derailed an offensive possession.
The combination of errors led to a 10-point deficit entering the final quarter.
“I’m so proud of this team and how we fought, and how we stayed connected with everything that went wrong,” Williams said.
“Not every game is going to go exactly how you want it,” Stafford said. “Sometimes you’re going to have to find ways to win football games, that’s what we did today.”
Stafford, Williams and the rest of the Rams’ offense certainly owes a debt of gratitude to the defense.

Los Angeles was playing without legendary defensive linemen Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, and still sacked Jalen Hurts four times. The Rams held the Eagles to only 172 total yards, including a prehistoric 68 passing yards. Philadelphia was additionally 0-for-12 on third-down attempts, and Los Angeles also held firm on fourth, turning the Eagles over on downs three separate times.

“I think a lot of teams would have folded in those situations, but our defense kept giving us a reason to believe,” McVay said. “There’s no style points in this league, but I do think a lot of growth can come from this.”

The Rams will certainly need to grow to reach the heights of their preseason expectations, as their season has been up and down so far. Los Angeles lost its season opener in Australia after a controversial travel plan, then came back to blow out the Giants in Week 2. But then the Rams crumbled in the second half of a 30-26 loss to the Broncos, all while the team has also dealt with injuries to key players.
The tests won’t stop for Los Angeles, however, as next up on the schedule are the 3-1 Buffalo Bills.
Said McVay about his team Sunday: “Tough times don’t last, tough people do.”

title: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson exits game vs. Titans with ankle injury
summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson missed the second half of the Ravens’ 24-18 win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday because of an ankle injury.
story: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson missed the second half of the Ravens’ 24-18 win against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday because of an ankle injury.

Jackson was on the sideline without a helmet during the Baltimore’s first possession of the third quarter, with the Ravens holding a 24-7 lead at the time. The team announced that he was questionable to return, but Jackson did not play another snap.
He was also seen wearing a boot on his left ankle after the game, according to ESPN.
Jackson was off to a hot start before leaving. He completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the first half. He also carried the ball twice for 20 yards.
He was tackled on the second to last play of the half and appeared to be favoring his ankle after going to the sideline. He was replaced by backup Tyler Huntley to start the third quarter.
Huntley finished the game completing 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards, and Baltimore did not score again.

Injuries have been an issue at times for Jackson, a two-time MVP. He missed four games last year, and the Ravens went only 2-2 in his absence. Baltimore finished the 2025 season 8-9 and missed the playoffs.

In 2021, Jackson missed five games, and the Ravens went 1-4 without him, missing the playoffs. The following season, he again missed five games and didn’t play in Baltimore’s first-round playoff loss.
For Subscribers

The Ravens entered this season with high expectations despite parting ways with previous head coach John Harbaugh. He was replaced by former Los Angeles Chargers defensive coordinator Jesse Minter, who was a defensive coach under Harbaugh in Baltimore from 2017 to 2020.
For Subscribers

The Ravens entered Sunday with a 2-1 record, defeating the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys, with their only loss coming against the New Orleans Saints. Baltimore is now tied with the Cleveland Browns at the top of the AFC North after Sunday’s win.

Jackson, 29, is in his ninth season with Baltimore, which selected him with the final pick of the first round in the 2018 NFL draft. Entering Sunday, he had thrown for 745 yards and four touchdowns this season and run for one more score.
Jackson is in the second to last year of a five-year, $260 million contract he signed in March 2023. He and the Ravens reportedly did not seriously discuss a long-term extension before this season.

title: Early indications suggest Flydubai co-pilot acted alone in attack, officials say
summary: Officials cautioned that the investigation remains in its early stages and that possible links to an organization or foreign government haven’t been definitively ruled out.
story: TEL AVIV — Early indications suggest the Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain and trying to seize control of an Israel-bound plane acted alone, rather than as part of a larger organization or on behalf of a foreign government, multiple U.S. officials briefed on the investigation and a former Israeli security official told NBC News.
The U.S. officials cautioned that the investigation into Wednesday’s midair attack remains at an early stage.

“The assessment is that he operated alone. Right now, it looks like a case of ‘lone wolf’ terrorism inspired by content found online,” said Shalom Ben Hanan, a former official in the Shin Bet, Israel’s domestic security agency.
“We still need to wait for the final investigation results to determine whether an organization or a state is behind it,” he added.

Emirati authorities, who are leading the investigation, said Saturday that the co-pilot attacked the captain with a crash ax and attempted to take control of the aircraft’s flight controls in an attempted terrorist attack.

The flight was carrying 174 mostly Israeli passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv. A crash was averted when crew members and passengers entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker, according to eyewitnesses and Israeli officials.

NBC News has identified the suspect as Omani citizen Hamam al-Hammami, based on information from multiple sources from three agencies briefed on the investigation and a diplomat in the Middle East. Authorities have not released his identity.
UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said Saturday that investigators were working to establish the incident’s “full circumstances, motives, and any links.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
The preliminary assessment comes after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Friday that investigators were examining whether the attacker had been sent by someone.

President Donald Trump also raised the possibility of Iranian involvement Thursday, threatening renewed strikes against Iran if it was behind the attack. A senior U.S. official briefed on the Israeli investigation previously told NBC News there were no indications that Iran directed or was involved in the attack.

The flight captain, Indian national Smit Machchhar, said Friday from a hospital in Abu Dhabi that he had been severely injured and could sense the aircraft descending before he managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers and crew to intervene.
“I was acting for my own life, but at the same time, I knew I couldn’t let all of them die,” he said on a video call released by India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Raf Sanchez and Paul Goldman reported from Tel Aviv and Tom Winter from New York.

title: Two dead, 35 wounded in shooting at Georgia block party
summary: The two who died were men ages 20 and 23. Dooly County authorities have yet to announce a suspect or a possible motive.
story: Two people were killed and 35 others were wounded in a shooting at a block party early Sunday in south-central Georgia.

The Georgia Bureau of Investigation said in a news release that shots were fired at about 1:25 a.m. in Vienna, a rural community about two hours south of Atlanta. NBC affiliate WALB of Albany described the event as a homecoming party.
Dooly County sheriff’s deputies were patrolling the party at the time, the bureau said. Two people were pronounced dead at the scene, and the wounded were taken to several regional hospitals.
For Subscribers
The bureau declined to say whether authorities had determined a motive or identified a suspect.
For Subscribers

“The investigation remains active and ongoing. At this time, no additional information is available for release,” Lydia Bullard, the bureau’s public affairs specialist, said in a statement to NBC News.

Brett Watts, the Dooly County coroner, said the two people who died were men ages 20 and 23. Each had a single gunshot wound, Watts said, though an autopsy by the medical examiner’s office, scheduled for Friday, could provide a fuller picture. He said the men’s families have been notified.

title: Cornell rape accuser faces threats demanding she drop her lawsuit, attorney says
summary: The accuser’s attorney said that women mistakenly identified as Jane Doe have also received threats and that he received one Sunday morning.
story: The woman who alleges she was sexually assaulted by Cornell University fraternity members has received threats pressuring her to drop her lawsuit, her attorney said Sunday.

Thomas Giuffra told CNN’s “State of the Union” that people attempting to unmask his client’s identity had also targeted at least three women mistakenly identified as her. The former Cornell student is identified as Jane Doe in court documents.
“She’s received multiple threats, and women who aren’t even Jane Doe receive threats,” Giuffra said. He added that he had received a threat Sunday morning.
For Subscribers
Giuffra did not identify those responsible or say whether the threats had been reported to law enforcement. He did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for more information about the threats.

Jane Doe filed a lawsuit last month against Cornell and seven Chi Phi fraternity members, alleging she was sexually assaulted over the course of hours on Oct. 19-20, 2024, while she was under the influence of ketamine, alcohol and marijuana.
For Subscribers

The allegations have sparked renewed scrutiny of the university’s and local authorities’ handling of the allegations. Gov. Kathy Hochul last week appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to consider whether criminal charges are appropriate.

NBC News reported Friday that Cornell police interviewed witnesses and received anonymous tips during their investigation in 2024, but Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten did not review that additional information before deciding not to pursue charges at the time. He has defended his decision, saying that Jane Doe’s initial six-page statement to police did not allege criminality.
Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said Saturday that the university must do better and that its board of trustees would announce an independent review of its handling of the case next week.

title: Search for 6 aboard medical jet enters second day after crash near Nantucket
summary: A Coast Guard official declined to say whether the mission had transitioned from rescue to recovery.
story: Authorities declined to speculate Sunday on what caused a medical evacuation jet to crash off Nantucket, Massachusetts, on Saturday morning as crews continue to search for the six missing passengers.

Rear Adm. Matt Lake, commander of the Coast Guard’s Northeast District, said at a news conference Sunday that Coast Guard crews, Massachusetts authorities and the New York National Guard’s air rescue wing have searched roughly 2,840 square miles over more than 53 hours.

“This is a large and demanding search area. Our crews are employing fixed-wing aircraft, helicopters, boats and cutters to search the area,” Lake said. He added that authorities hope to use sonar to search the seabed.

He declined to say whether the mission had shifted from rescue to recovery, which would mean no survivors are expected. He also declined to provide the passengers’ names or ages “out of respect to the families and next of kin.”
The U.S. Coast Guard launched a search Saturday morning and found a debris field approximately 20 miles off the coast of Massachusetts’ Nantucket island later that day.

Air traffic controllers lost contact with the jet early Saturday as it flew from Bermuda to Boston. One controller asked the crew whether it was declaring an emergency and “coming in blind,” according to audio obtained by NBC News.
The six people on board were four Canadians and two Bermudians. A source familiar with the matter told NBC News the Bermudians were a patient and the patient’s son.
The Bermudian government said Saturday that it was in contact with the families of those on board. The Coast Guard said it had notified next of kin.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The flight was scheduled to last less than two hours, according to data from FlightAware, a site that tracks flights in real time. The jet took off from L.F. Wade International Airport in Bermuda at about 12:40 a.m. and was due to land at Boston Logan International Airport just before 1:30 a.m. Bermuda is a British overseas territory in the North Atlantic, about 775 miles from Boston.
At around 1:05 a.m., FlightAware shows the jet dropping from 24,000 feet to 11,000 feet over the Atlantic Ocean.

The plane was operated by Latitude Air Ambulance, an Ontario, Canada-based medical evacuation company that arranges private flights for sick or injured patients. According to the company’s website, a typical flight is staffed by two pilots and two medical crew members and carries a patient and an escort. The Gulfstream jet that crashed Saturday was equipped to carry full ICU medical equipment and supplies.
Lake said Sunday that investigators would likely try to locate the plane’s flight recorder system, or “black box,” which is designed to preserve evidence after a crash.
“There’s no indications that we found a black box. But again, it’s very difficult because that debris is extensive,” Lake said.

title: Sen. John Kennedy says he’s considering running for president
summary: The Louisiana Republican said he hasn’t decided and that right now he’s planning to run for re-election in 2028.
story: Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that he is considering a run for president in 2028.
Asked by moderator Kristen Welker whether he was thinking about running for president, Kennedy replied, “Yeah.”
“My plans right now are to run for re-election, but as I’ve said before, if I don’t think I can be effective in the Senate anymore, I would consider it,” he said.

A slew of politicians on both sides of the aisle have acknowledged that they are considering running for president in 2028 or have declined to rule out the possibility. None, though, have formally announced yet that they are running. Kennedy, too, said that he has not made a decision.

“On my side of the aisle, if a bunch of goobers run, and I think they’re goobers and one of the goobers might win, and I think I could do a better job, I would consider running,” he said. “But right now, I’m running for re-election.”
Kennedy is up for re-election in 2028.

Vice President JD Vance is widely considered a likely presidential candidate in 2028. Kennedy, though, declined to talk about Vance when asked why voters should pick the senator over the vice president.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“I’m not going to talk about another potential candidate,” he said. “I’m just not there yet.”
He added that he thinks “it’ll be good for both parties to have a full field.”
President Donald Trump has previously floated both Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio as potential successors. In September, Rubio said he has “no plans at this time” to run for president.

NBC News previously reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has talked about potentially running for president in 2028, which a Defense Department spokesperson denied. Separately, Vance told NBC News last week that it was “really obvious to me” that Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, was running for president in 2028.
The 2028 presidential election will be the first time since 2012 in which Trump will not be the Republican nominee.

title: Rahm Emanuel says Democrats should focus on ethics reforms rather than impeaching Trump
summary: Democrats have publicly weighed whether they should pursue impeaching Trump for a third time.
story: Former White House chief of staff Rahm Emanuel called on Democratic lawmakers Sunday to set aside plans to impeach President Donald Trump if they win a majority in the House, pushing them instead to pass an ethics reform package.

Asked directly on NBC News’ “Meet the Press” whether Democrats should take up impeachment in January if they take the House gavel, Emanuel said: “Short answer: No, because it’s not going anywhere, and it’s going to be a food fight, and it’s just going to be we return to the politics of fighting.”

Emanuel, who served as President Barack Obama’s first chief of staff, proposed that Democrats could instead “pass an ethics package” to address the corruption he said is taking place in the Trump administration.

In a September NBC News poll, government corruption emerged as the second-highest-rated issue voters were concerned about ahead of November’s midterm elections. On the airwaves, tackling government corruption and banning congressional stock trading has been a top issue in campaign ads from Democrats and Republicans.
Should Democrats take back the House, Emanuel said, they should “hold [the Trump administration] accountable and then pass an ethics package.”

“You’re never going to get an impeachment,” he added. “Then if you do that, you just basically prove all Washington is what the American people think. It’s Disneyland on the Potomac. Deliver the change. Deliver a comprehensive ethics package that uses the investigations to then deliver change.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

In September, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who could be speaker of the House if Democrats win a majority in Congress’ lower chamber in November, said his party’s top priorities would be to tackle healthcare costs and affordability.
Jeffries has refrained from weighing in on calls from some fellow Democrats that the party should impeach the president if they take control of the House.

In a June interview with “Meet the Press,” Jeffries told moderator Kristen Welker when asked about a potential impeachment: “We haven’t ruled anything in or ruled anything out in terms of accountability. What we have said is that our focus is going to be to make life more affordable for the American people. We have to drive down the high cost of living.”
Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., last month told “Meet the Press” that impeaching Trump was not a “taboo” topic.

“Everybody on our side understands that impeachment is a critical tool in the toolbox for constitutional self-defense against a president acting like a king, an imperious, lawless, arrogant king,” the Maryland lawmaker said, adding later in the interview: “Impeachment is not a taboo with us. It’s not a fetish with us.”
Trump was impeached twice in his first term but not convicted.
Emanuel, who was also a two-term mayor of Chicago, is widely speculated to be considering a run for president in 2028.

The New York Times reported last month that he has been a crucial behind-the-scenes player in the 2026 midterms, helping his party recruit candidates and offering advice to party leaders and candidates.

The 2028 contest for the Democratic presidential nomination is expected to yield a crowded field of candidates, with nearly a dozen Democratic governors and members of Congress also fueling speculation that they’ll run.

Asked Sunday on “Meet the Press” whether he’ll run for president in 2028, Emanuel demurred, outlining affordability and building a positive vision for the future as the two most important issues facing the next president.

“We’ve had two presidents back to back who’ve actually tried to restore a past that’s not coming back. Let’s build a future that we — actually, every American and every community in America is part of,” Emanuel said.
